#93636. Industry News: Scientists discover a bizarre paradox among endangered penguins

Industry News: Scientists discover a bizarre paradox among endangered penguins

📅 15 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 6 min read (1268 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Sciencedaily

⏱️ ~6 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • A fresh study from the University of Otago, Ōtākou Whakaihu Waka, has revealed a surprising divide in the fortunes of one of New Zealand's least understood penguin species.
  • Published in PLOS ONE, the research found that one population has remained stable for at least 25 years, while the other has declined by more than 40 percent over the past three decades.
  • In a recent development, the study was led by Dr.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

A fresh study from the University of Otago, Ōtākou Whakaihu Waka, has revealed a surprising divide in the fortunes of one of New Zealand's least understood penguin species. Although Erect-crested penguins breed in just two remote island groups, their populations are experiencing dramatically different outcomes.

Published in PLOS ONE, the research found that one population has remained stable for at least 25 years, while the other has declined by more than 40 percent over the past three decades.

In a recent development, the study was led by Dr. Thomas Mattern of the Tawaki Project, which brings together scientists from the university's Departments of Zoology and Marine Science. Researchers also collaborated with the Antarctic Research Trust and the Global Penguin Society.

Drone Surveys Reveal a Surprising Penguin Population Divide.

Erect-crested penguins breed exclusively on the Bounty and Antipodes islands, two isolated island groups located approximately 800 kilometers southeast of Fresh Zealand's South Island.

According to recent reports, to determine how many penguins remain, researchers conducted extensive drone surveys between 2022 and 2024. They photographed and counted every breeding colony across both island groups, producing the first comprehensive population survey of the entire species.

"The results overturn a long-standing assumption," Dr. Mattern indicates.

"The tiny Bounty Islands, at just 50 hectares, were found to hold almost as many breeding pairs (about 27,800) as the Antipodes Islands (about 29,800), even though the latter is 40 times larger and historically considered the species' stronghold.".

It has been revealed that the difference in population trends was even more unexpected. Despite their small size, the Bounty Islands have maintained a relatively consistent number of breeding penguins for decades. Meanwhile, the much larger Antipodes Islands have experienced a substantial decline.

"Comparing the newly introduced counts with historical records going back to the mid-1990s, the Bounty Islands population has remained essentially unchanged for at least 25 years.

"The Antipodes Islands population, by contrast, has declined by more than 40 percent since 1995.".

Why Are Penguins Disappearing From the Antipodes Islands?

In a recent development, researchers believe several overlapping pressures may explain why the two populations are heading in opposite directions. Natural predators, increasingly destructive storms, and differences in where the birds travel and feed could all be contributing.

Industry observers note that one particularly troubling factor involves skuas, native subantarctic birds that prey on penguin eggs and chicks. As penguin colonies become smaller, the birds lose some of the protection that comes from nesting together in large numbers.

"As Antipodes colonies have shrunk over recent decades, the collective defense they once provided against native subantarctic bird, the skua, a natural predator of eggs and chicks, has weakened, allowing predation losses to increase and colonies to fragment further.".

Co-author Dr. Klemens Pütz of the Antarctic Research Trust suggests that changes involving another penguin species may have intensified this pressure.

Eastern Rockhopper penguins suffered a "catastrophically" severe population collapse during the second half of the 20th century. Similar declines occurred across their Southern Ocean breeding range, likely driven by warming ocean waters. Today, fewer than 1,000 breeding pairs remain on the Antipodes Islands.

"As Rockhoppers disappeared, skuas may have turned to Erect-crested penguin eggs and chicks instead," Dr. Pütz notes.

Stronger Storms and Different Migration Routes Add to the Threat.

Predators are not the only challenge facing the Antipodes penguins. Increasingly powerful storms, consistent with wider climate trends across the Southern Ocean, have caused landslides that break up breeding colonies and leave the birds more vulnerable.

Differences in ocean habitats and seasonal movements may also help explain why the two populations have experienced such contrasting outcomes.

In a recent development, according to Dr. Mattern, penguins breeding on the Antipodes Islands migrate considerable distances into the Antarctic Polar Frontal Zone when the breeding season ends. In contrast, birds from the Bounty Islands remain closer to their nesting grounds, where the surrounding waters are more sheltered and may offer more abundant food.

These differences could leave the two populations exposed to very different environmental pressures, despite belonging to the same species.

The Strange Paradox of Schrödinger's Penguin.

The researchers have named this unusual situation "Schrödinger's Penguin," drawing inspiration from the famous physics thought experiment involving a cat inside a sealed box.

Industry observers note that in that experiment, the cat is imagined to be both alive and dead until the box is opened and its condition is observed. But Dr. Mattern explains that the penguin discovery turns the familiar concept around.

"With Schrödinger's cat, opening the box settles the question one way or the other.

"With Erect-crested penguins, it's the opposite. From a distance, without proper surveys, everyone assumed there was a single answer for the whole species.

"Once we actually opened the metaphorical box and looked, we found there wasn't one state at all, but two: stable on the Bounty Islands, declining on the Antipodes Islands.".

In other words, looking at the species as a whole can conceal what is happening within individual populations. Only by examining both island groups separately did researchers uncover how dramatically their circumstances differ.

A Hidden Conservation Crisis for Endangered Penguins.

Industry observers note that the Erect-crested penguin is currently one of only four penguin species worldwide classified as "Endangered" on the International Union for Conservation of Nature Red List. Another New Zealand penguin, the hoiho/yellow-eyed penguin, shares that designation.

According to recent reports, however, the two species have received very different levels of attention. While the plight of the hoiho has attracted ongoing public interest and conservation efforts, the Erect-crested penguin has remained relatively overlooked.

It has been revealed that dr. Mattern explains that the species' current conservation classification relies on population estimates from the 1970s that were considerably inflated. When the new survey results are considered, the "Endangered" designation remains broadly appropriate for the declining Antipodes population, but not for the stable Bounty Islands population.

This creates a difficult conservation dilemma. If the two populations are combined into a single assessment, the species' overall threat classification could actually improve, even though one population continues to decline sharply.

"Averaged across both populations, the global ranking would actually improve to "Vulnerable," masking the severity of the Antipodes decline, and downplaying how exposed the Bounty Islands, likely the species' last secure stronghold, are to industrial fishing.".

The researchers warn that a more favorable overall classification could create a misleading impression of security. Although the Bounty Islands population remains stable, it may still face significant threats, particularly from industrial fishing activity.

In a recent development, "A single, ostensibly improved threat ranking is like putting the lid back on Schrödinger's box, trading a convenient illusion for the stronger protection the Bounty Islands population actually needs," Dr. Mattern claims.

The findings highlight why conservation efforts must account for the circumstances of individual populations rather than relying exclusively on a species' global status. For Erect-crested penguins, recognizing the differences between the two island groups could be essential to protecting their future.

Recent findings suggest that the study received funding from the Vontobel Foundation (Switzerland) through the Antarctic Research Trust and from the Global Penguin Society. The research was carried out under permits issued by the Newly introduced Zealand Department of Conservation.

💡 Key Takeaways

  • Recent findings suggest that A Long March 2F rocket, topped with the Shenzhou-24 crew spacecraft, was rolled out to the pad at Jiuquan Satellite Launch Center in northwest China, on Tuesday (Nov.
  • The 191-foot-tall (58 meters) rocket was transferred 0.93 miles (1.5 kilometers) from a vertical integration building to the pad over the course of around two hours, starting around 4 a.m.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

China's space station is set to receive its first foreign astronaut.

Recent findings suggest that A Long March 2F rocket, topped with the Shenzhou-24 crew spacecraft, was rolled out to the pad at Jiuquan Satellite Launch Center in northwest China, on Tuesday (Nov. 17), with launch expected in the next week.

The 191-foot-tall (58 meters) rocket was transferred 0.93 miles (1.5 kilometers) from a vertical integration building to the pad over the course of around two hours, starting around 4 a.m. EST (0900 GMT, or 5 p.m. Beijing Time), according to China Central Television (CCTV).

China's human spaceflight agency, CMSA, stated that all facilities and equipment at the launch site are in good condition, adding that the launch is scheduled to take place in the coming days, without providing a date.

CMSA typically holds a press conference at Jiuquan a day ahead of launch, during which the crew for the mission is revealed to the public. This time, one of the three crew members will, for the first time, be an international astronaut. One of two Pakistani astronaut candidates will fly to the Tiangong space station on Shenzhou-24, marking a first both for China's outpost and for Pakistan, which will see one its astronauts reach orbit for the first time.

Though public details are sparse, it is thought that the Pakistani astronaut, operating as a payload specialist, will stay aboard Tiangong for around a week, returning home on the departing Shenzhou-23 spacecraft.

It has been revealed that one of the three Shenzhou-23 astronauts — who are approaching the end of their six-month-long mission, having launched on May 24 — will stay aboard Tiangong for another half a year. This will provide the international visitor with a seat home on Shenzhou-23, and allow a Chinese astronaut to make the country's first year-long stay in orbit. This extra-long mission will supply China with data on physiology ahead of crewed lunar flights and other long-duration missions.

Industry observers note that china approved its human spaceflight program in 1992 and launched its first orbital crewed mission in 2003, with Yang Liwei becoming the first Chinese national in space. The country then completed the three-module Tiangong space station in late 2022 and has kept the orbital outpost constantly crewed ever since, with rotating six-month-long missions with brief handovers between crews.

Shenzhou-24 will be China's 18th crewed mission and will mark the first time a foreign national is flying on a Shenzhou spacecraft. China is also looking to double the size of Tiangong in the coming years, potentially opening the way to further international missions and space tourist visits.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Alex Consani is ready for a spin around Vice City.

With the supermodel lending her voice to Grand Theft Auto VI—which is poised to be the biggest video game of the year after making $3.79 billion in preorder and first-day sales, according to parent company Take Two—it was only appropriate that she channel that car vibe into her clutch look for the game’s launch party.

Consani buckled up for the Nov. 18 event at the Gekko restaurant in Miami wearing a short dress from Paris-based label Sevali’s spring 2025 collection that was made out of upcycled seatbelts. The belts crisscrossed around the 23-year-old’s svelte figure, coming to a click—literally—with a buckle that was strapped across her shoulder.

The Victoria’s Secret model completed her look with clear kitten heels and her long blonde hair parted down the middle and flowing behind her.

In the newly released video game, Consani can be heard as a DJ for the in-game radio station Flash FM alongside singer Robyn. The two play songs from the likes of Olivia Rodrigo, Charli XCX, Zara Larsson and more as they put their commentary into high gear.

After playing Rodrigo’s “good 4 u,” Consani can be heard saying in a clip posted from the game, “How do you even fumble a baddie like Olivia?”.

According to recent reports, she also had some love for Charli XCX, saying, “Whatever Charli XCX does, she’s my medicine. That is my f--king doctor, y’all.”.

Sources indicate that as for Larsson? After playing the Swedish singer’s hit “Fast Emotion,” Consani commented, “God, I love Zara so much.”.

Of course, the model isn’t the only star to lend her voice to GTA VI, with Bad Bunny coming in as host of Latin radio Cocoteo FM, PinkPantheress DJing the indie dance station Stockyard FM, “Weird” Al Yankovic hosting the ’80s station Vice City FM, Morgan Wallen and Lana Del Rey co-hosting Back Country Radio and Rolling Stones guitarist Keith Richards playing his part as DJ Keith on Gloriana Blues Radio.

Grand Theft Auto VI marks the latest installment in the long-running video game series, coming out 13 years after the record-breaking Grand Theft Auto V.

The fresh game features characters like Jason Duval and Lucia Caminos as they take part in fan-favorite activities from previous games like car-jackings, shootouts, street-racing, robberies, swimming, jet-skiing, sky-diving, visiting the strip club and, yes, even petting dogs. GTA 6 is set around locations inspired by Floria, allowing players new playable vehicles like kayaks and airboats to roam around the new locale.

💡 Key Takeaways

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

During talks on ending the war in Ukraine, Russian representatives in Abu Dhabi presented a document containing far-reaching demands, The Latest York Times reports.

Dated November 10, the document reportedly calls not only for an end to Western arms deliveries to Ukraine but also for NATO to withdraw its troops and bases and move them back to where they were in 1997.

The year 1997 refers to the NATO alliance before its first eastward expansion, according to the Kremlin. At the time, NATO had 16 members. Poland, the Czech Republic and Hungary had already been invited to join but did not formally become members of the defense alliance until two years later. In the following years, more countries in Central, Eastern and Southeastern Europe joined, followed most recently by countries in Scandinavia. Today, NATO has 32 member states in Europe and North America.

According to the report, Russia is not explicitly demanding that Central and Eastern European countries leave, but rather that the NATO alliance end its military presence in those countries.

According to recent reports, A withdrawal of NATO troops and bases from member states that joined the alliance after 1997 would significantly weaken their defense capabilities. For example, since 2004, NATO allies, including Germany, have taken turns policing the airspace over Estonia, Latvia and Lithuania.

Sources indicate that because the Baltic states do not have fighter jets of their own for independent air policing, NATO provides the capability. Since 2026, the mission has been part of a broader air defense presence. The planned deployment of the German Lithuania Brigade, which is expected to be fully operational by the end of 2027, would also have to be halted.

In a recent development, in Romania, meanwhile, the Mihail Kogalniceanu Air Base near Constanța on the Black Sea is presently being expanded. Once completed, it is set to become Europe's largest NATO air base by area — even larger than Ramstein in Germany.

According to recent reports, "Under no circumstances will we allow anyone to establish latest security rules for this part of the world over the heads of Poland and Europe," Polish Prime Minister Donald Tusk told TVP World. His Bulgarian counterpart, Rumen Radev, called a NATO withdrawal "unthinkable and unrealistic." No country should be forced by external pressure to reverse its decision on which alliance to join.

Estonian Prime Minister Kristen Michal also rejected any Russian say in changes to Europe's security order: "We have nothing to discuss with Russia about Europe's security order; it is working well.".

The strong rejection from the capitals of NATO's eastern members, however, masks fears along the alliance's eastern flank that a deal between Washington and Moscow could turn their security into a bargaining chip.

Recent findings suggest that in the event of an armed attack on a NATO member, the other alliance members are obligated under Article 5 to come to its aid. Each member decides for itself what measures it considers necessary, which may include the use of military force.

Recent findings suggest that for the mutual defense commitment to deter a potential aggressor, that country must believe NATO can intervene militarily quickly and effectively in a crisis. The deployment of allied troops along the eastern flank serves precisely this purpose. A withdrawal would make defense more difficult and could lead Russia to believe that an attack on NATO territory would involve fewer risks for Moscow.

As part of their security framework, European countries have agreed that states are free to decide which alliances they wish to join. NATO points to Article 10 of its founding treaty, which enshrines its open-door policy for European countries. The 1997 NATO-Russia Founding Act also explicitly stated that neither side had the right to veto the other's decisions.

Back in November 1990, the participating states of the Conference on Security and Cooperation in Europe (CSCE), including the Soviet Union, had already agreed in the Charter of Paris to respect each country's freedom to choose its own security arrangements.

During the negotiations surrounding German reunification, then-US Secretary of State James Baker and German Foreign Minister Hans-Dietrich Genscher used language that suggested putting limits on NATO's eastward expansion.

Their remarks came during discussions about unified Germany's membership in NATO and the possible deployment of NATO forces on the territory of the former East Germany. However, no written, legally binding general promise was ever agreed that NATO would never expand to include other former Warsaw Pact countries.

Industry observers note that in the 1997 NATO-Russia Founding Act, both sides declared that they no longer considered each other adversaries. NATO stated that, under the security conditions prevailing at the time and in the foreseeable future, it intended to ensure its collective defense through reinforcement rather than the additional permanent stationing of "substantial combat forces." The agreement explicitly gave Moscow no veto over NATO decisions.

In the 1994 Budapest Memorandum, Russia, the United States and the United Kingdom reaffirmed their commitment to respect Ukraine's independence and existing borders and to refrain from the use of force. These assurances were linked to Ukraine's decision to give up its nuclear weapons. However, the memorandum did not oblige the United States or the United Kingdom to defend Ukraine militarily in the event of an attack. NATO membership was not addressed at the time.

Just over two months before Russia's full-scale invasion of Ukraine, the Kremlin presented two draft treaties to the United States and NATO. In them, Russia demanded an end to further NATO enlargement. The draft agreement with NATO also proposed that Russia and NATO members that had already joined the alliance as of May 27, 1997, refrain from deploying additional troops or weapons on the territory of other European countries beyond the levels stationed there on that date.

Security guarantees for the postwar period and a future security framework for Europe were also on the agenda in Abu Dhabi. Negotiating NATO troop deployments and alliance enlargement alongside an end to the war in Ukraine would give Moscow additional leverage. Russia has long maintained that the "root causes" of the war must be addressed. The Kremlin includes NATO enlargement and the alliance's military presence in Eastern Europe among those causes.

Industry observers note that so far, no significant Western player has expressed willingness to accept Russia's demands in Abu Dhabi. On the contrary, former Polish intelligence coordinator Stanislaw Zaryn viewed the talks as an attempt to buy time and weaken the West ahead of another confrontation.

Don Bluth on the future of animation and AI: Thats definitely a road I dont want to travel on

⏱️ ~9 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • According to recent reports, for children of the '80s and '90s, Don Bluth was a major influence on how we saw the world.
  • According to recent reports, social media is evergreen with fans remembering the tender moments of Littlefoot and his tree star, or the terrifying ones, like Fievel or Mrs.
  • In an interview with Mashable, Bluth said watching the finished doc "brought tears to [his] eyes," because it refreshed memories of his colleagues.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

According to recent reports, for children of the '80s and '90s, Don Bluth was a major influence on how we saw the world. With movies like The Secret of NIMH, An American Tail, The Land Before Time, All Dogs Go to Heaven, and Anastasia, this American animator offered us realms of adventure, with plucky heroes as well as villains so fantastically frightening that we carry the thrill of it all with us decades later.

According to recent reports, social media is evergreen with fans remembering the tender moments of Littlefoot and his tree star, or the terrifying ones, like Fievel or Mrs. Brisby being chased down by monstrous, roaring, ravenous cats. Now, for fans latest and old, filmmakers Dave LaMattina and Chad N. Walker offer Don Bluth: Somewhere Out There, a documentary that explores the life and work of the innovative animator through his own words.

In an interview with Mashable, Bluth said watching the finished doc "brought tears to [his] eyes," because it refreshed memories of his colleagues. Together, they pursued animation not for the money but for the art and a deep desire to create something meaningful for future generations. Yet, when asked about his legacy, Bluth is quick to look back on the path that led him to his work.

He began by speaking of Winsor McCay, the father of American animation. In a wistful storyteller tone, Bluth recounted how a little boy witnessed the "magic" of the 1914 short film Gertie the Dinosaur, in which a pencil-sketched brontosaurus comes to life. This little boy was so inspired that he'd grow up to make his own animated short featuring a mouse named Mickey.

According to recent reports, that little boy, of course, was Walt Disney, who would go on to make 1937's Snow White and the Seven Dwarfs, the first animated feature film produced in the United States. That movie would go on to inspire a young Bluth, who'd direct his first animated feature in 1982 with The Secret of NIMH.

This path of inspiration to iconic art wasn't as direct a line as you might think.

Yes, Bluth scored a dream job, working at Disney Animation studio for 10 years on films like Sleeping Beauty, Robin Hood, and The Rescuers. But after Disney's death in 1966, Bluth and 17 other Disney animators feared the studio had lost their way, creatively.

Industry observers note that he told Mashable he'd invite these artists to his home on weekends, where they'd draw together to develop innovative pitches for their corporate bosses. When they were shot down, Bluth — along with Gary Goldman and John Pomeroy — built their own company, Don Bluth Productions, to "see if we could do better than they were doing." For this, Bluth remembered, "We were called traitors.".

Recent findings suggest that that's not how Bluth saw his team. "[These] wonderful people had the courage to leave their jobs and security and go out there and try and do something great," he remarked, "not just to feed their egos, but something they felt helped them grow up. And they wanted to give back.".

It was not an easy journey, as Don Bluth: Somewhere Out There details, revealing the highs and lows of Bluth's most beloved and worst-reviewed productions, as well as the wildly popular video game Dragon's Lair. In our interview, he spoke repeatedly about how the doc filled him with gratitude as he looked back for the filmmakers' interviews.

According to recent reports, to Mashable, he reflected, "What happened after so many movies, All Dogs Go to Heaven, American Tail, working with Steven Spielberg on both of those pictures, and George Lucas [on The Land Before Time], [it] became really, really obvious to us that we were doing the right thing [by] writing the right stories, and trying to make something that would move people's lives for the better — not just to pat our own backs and say, 'Look what we did.' [We were making] something that would help maybe children grow up and have some degree of morality about them. So then, that was our goal in everything.".

Recent findings suggest that in Somewhere Out There, the rise of computer animation — which Bluth refers to as "3D animation" — came as a devastating blow to the animator, who'd spent his life developing the skills of hand-drawn 2D animation. To this day, Bluth still advocates for the artistry of hand-drawn animation.

"The way I look at this is animation in the 2D form is people, armed with a pencil in their hands, have to be able to draw," he explained, "and they also have to be able to act. And they have to have feelings about story.".

To Bluth, CGI movies aren't animation. "3D animation is puppetry," he said, adding, "[With 3D animation,] you drop your pencil. You put your hands on a keyboard, and you make a wireframe puppet act.".

According to recent reports, bluth shared several of his complaints about the look of 3D animation, saying, "To me, it looks very plastic... The colors are muted, and they're trying to put shading in there, trying to look more like a live-action picture." He asked, "Why are we trying to get to a place which looks more real?" adding, "That isn't the purpose at all of 2D [animation]. The purpose is to take you to a magical world. 2D is trying to make audiences come to our own world.".

Industry observers note that noting the animation industry changed forever with the massive success of 1995's Toy Story, Bluth stated, "Toy Story [movies] were quite fun to watch, but they didn't make me feel anything very deep. And animation is intended to do that, particularly with Walt Disney pictures. Snow White, Bambi, [and] Pinocchio — those pictures did something to change the way you thought and help you grow up in a way that was really good. And they did it in such a beautiful way.".

It was when Disney Studios, post-Walt, moved away from these tenets that Bluth and his colleagues set out on their own. He said, "We left the Disney Studio because it was leaving out the morality statements and leaving out all the beautiful colors and everything.".

In terms of what recent animated films impressed Bluth, he said, "I liked Klaus a lot," commending Sergio Pablos' inventive Christmas tale, which employs hand-drawn animation with a unique visual style.

It has been revealed that bluth also enjoyed Pete Docter's 2009 Pixar hit Up. "That was totally in 3D," he noted, "but it had a great story. For my taste, it went on too long. You know, the story was really about this couple promising each other they would go back to some place in their life, and she died. So, the man, true to the promise, tries to fulfill that [by taking their house on the journey]. So, I love that.".

Overall though, Bluth lamented, "Animation has become an advertisement for sugar cereal and whatever. There are more advertisements on animation than there are actually animated characters. The animated characters are just simply little puppets that jump up and down and tell one-line jokes. So, that's not good. Now, the last laugh is about to hit us like a tsunami; that is AI.".

Through the stories of Russian Jewish immigrant Fievel Mousekewitz, the widowed mother of four Mrs. Brisby, the orphaned brontosaurus Littlefoot, and rogue mutt Charlie B. Barkin, Bluth was striving to create stories that would inspire children to be good and creative, as Disney's movies had done for him. He doesn't see a future where AI can provide such mindful, moral guidance.

In a recent development, "It seems like AI is able to do wonderful, wonderful things," Bluth mused, "except AI is a machine, and it has no soul. It will borrow or steal, if you will, from everything that it knows, and give you what you ask for. But where's the creativity?".

It has been revealed that "AI is a borrower," Bluth explained. "When you enter what you'd like to see, it searches all over and borrows it from other artists, puts it together. It shows you on screen. Now, you can then make corrections. It can do all that, but it is still a machine. It doesn't ask you, 'Well, what is right and wrong? What is evil and good? What do you want me to say?' The machine can't do that.".

Sources indicate that he continued, "The only thing you can do is go back to human beings and say, 'Don't replace human beings with machines.' They're the ones who have a heart, who have a soul, and probably have a Creator. So, there's a bigger picture that's going on than just animation on a screen.".

Sources indicate that "AI has no soul," Bluth concluded. "It hasn't a clue how to write anything. Everything that you're going to see on your screen has been stolen from other artists.".

He allowed that some AI might be "stunningly beautiful," but "you'll find that it doesn't affect your heart the way you feel… They're not artists that are doing the AI. Many of them don't understand the art of acting or anything. So, what everything looks like in AI animation that I've seen, it all looks like slow motion, and it looks unreal. So, that's definitely a road I don't want to travel on.".

"I read somewhere where someone said something that stuck in my head," he mused, paraphrasing Oscar Wilde's The Portrait of Dorian Gray. "There are many people who know the price of everything but the value of nothing. And I certainly hope that's not where we're going.".

Industry News: Physicists use laser light to unlock a crystal's hidden electrical powers

⏱️ ~4 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • Physicists at Auburn University have discovered how to use brief bursts of laser light to organize tiny electrical regions hidden inside a crystal.
  • The research was led by Wencan Jin, the Thomas and Jean Walter Endowed Associate Professor in Auburn's Department of Physics, and graduate student Mohamed Kandil.
  • According to recent reports, the researchers investigated a modified version of strontium titanate, a material with an unusual combination of electrical characteristics.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Physicists at Auburn University have discovered how to use brief bursts of laser light to organize tiny electrical regions hidden inside a crystal. Their findings shed new light on a mystery that has puzzled researchers for decades and demonstrate how lasers can influence the material's electrical behavior. The breakthrough could eventually help scientists explore faster ways to process and store information.

The research was led by Wencan Jin, the Thomas and Jean Walter Endowed Associate Professor in Auburn's Department of Physics, and graduate student Mohamed Kandil. Their paper, "Optical Poling of a Quantum Ferroelectric Metal across the Order-Disorder Phase Transition," received an Editors' Suggestion designation from Physical Review Letters. Scientists at Japan's National Institute of Advanced Industrial Science and Technology produced the crystals used in the study.

A Decades-Old Mystery Hidden Inside a Crystal.

According to recent reports, the researchers investigated a modified version of strontium titanate, a material with an unusual combination of electrical characteristics. Although electrons can travel through the crystal, it also contains extremely small regions with positive and negative electrical sides. Known as polar nanoregions, these microscopic "islands" can point in different directions or become aligned with one another. Understanding how and why this alignment occurs is essential to explaining the material's properties and learning how to manipulate them.

Scientists have spent decades trying to determine what happens when these regions become organized. One possibility is that atoms move together to produce the polarized state. Another is that the tiny electrical islands are already there and simply begin pointing in the same direction as temperatures fall. The distinction is similar to the difference between assembling a group of people and asking people who are already gathered to turn and face the same way. Because the regions are extraordinarily small and produce very weak signals, determining which explanation is correct has been a persistent challenge.

Laser Experiments Reveal How Electrical Order Emerges.

To investigate, the Auburn researchers developed an exceptionally sensitive system that uses lasers to measure subtle changes in the crystal. By studying how the material altered incoming light, they were able to monitor the orientation of its electrical regions while repeatedly heating and cooling the sample.

The measurements revealed a clear pattern. At warmer temperatures, the tiny regions pointed in seemingly random directions. When the crystal cooled, however, they began adopting preferred orientations. This behavior provided compelling evidence that the electrical islands existed before becoming aligned, supporting the explanation that cooling organizes regions already present in the material.

A Flash of Light Creates Order in a Trillionth of a Second.

It has been revealed that the team went beyond observing this natural process. Researchers also demonstrated that short laser pulses could temporarily align the electrical islands, even at higher temperatures when the regions would ordinarily remain disorganized. Using an optical measurement, they were able to detect the pattern produced by the laser light.

The effect was extraordinarily brief, lasting approximately one picosecond, or one trillionth of a second. Nevertheless, the ability to create and detect this electrical alignment using light provides a promising approach for studying how information might be controlled at extremely high speeds.

Three Years of Experiments Lead to a Breakthrough.

Industry observers note that achieving these results required considerable patience and technical refinement. The collaboration began at the 2023 American Physical Society March Meeting, where Jin met Japanese researchers capable of producing the specialized crystals needed for the experiments.

Back at Auburn, the team spent almost a year refining its equipment before it could reliably detect the weak optical signals from the tiny electrical regions. The next obstacle was even more demanding: measuring the extremely short interval during which laser illumination caused the regions to align.

In a recent development, "The breakthrough came in 2025, when Mohamed finally observed the disordered polar regions becoming aligned under laser illumination," Jin said. "Seeing that signal emerge was a thrilling moment for the team.".

The achievement also represents an key personal milestone for Kandil, whose first published research paper reflects three years of dedicated experimental work.

It has been revealed that "This experiment has truly been Mohamed's odyssey," Jin said. "It took him three years of dedication to complete the work and achieve his first publication.".

Fresh Possibilities for Ultrafast Information Technology.

The discovery provides important evidence about how electrical order develops in this unusual crystal while also establishing a method for manipulating that order with light. Rather than simply observing the material's internal behavior, researchers can now briefly influence its microscopic electrical patterns and detect the resulting changes.

Sources indicate that although practical applications remain a future possibility, the experiments offer a new way to investigate the rapid electrical processes occurring inside quantum materials. By revealing how light can control these previously elusive patterns, the Auburn researchers have opened another avenue for exploring technologies that could one day transform how information is processed and stored.

Erdogan's political fate may be determined by Turkey's Kurds

📅 03 Apr 2023 | ⏱️ 8 min read (1521 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: CNN

⏱️ ~8 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • Turkey’s persecuted pro-Kurdish party has emerged as a kingmaker in the country’s upcoming election, playing a decisive role that may just tip the balance enough to unseat two-decade ruler Recep Tayyip Erdogan.
  • In a key setback to the Turkish president and leader of the Justice and Development Party (AK Party), the pro-Kurdish Peoples’ Democratic Party (HDP) last month revealed that it would not put forward its own presidential candidate, a move analysts say allows its supporters to vote for Erdogan’s main rival.
  • Industry observers note that “We are facing a turning point that will shape the future of Turkey and (its) society,” remarked the HDP in a statement on March 23.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Turkey’s persecuted pro-Kurdish party has emerged as a kingmaker in the country’s upcoming election, playing a decisive role that may just tip the balance enough to unseat two-decade ruler Recep Tayyip Erdogan.

In a key setback to the Turkish president and leader of the Justice and Development Party (AK Party), the pro-Kurdish Peoples’ Democratic Party (HDP) last month revealed that it would not put forward its own presidential candidate, a move analysts say allows its supporters to vote for Erdogan’s main rival.

Industry observers note that “We are facing a turning point that will shape the future of Turkey and (its) society,” remarked the HDP in a statement on March 23. “To fulfill our historical responsibility against the one-man rule, we will not field a presidential candidate in (the) May 14 elections.”.

It is a twist of irony for the Turkish strongman, who spent the better half of the past decade cracking down on the party after it began chipping away at his voter base. Its former leader Selahattin Demirtas has been in prison for nearly seven years and the party faces possible closure by a court for suspected collusion with the militant Kurdistan Workers’ Party (PKK) and affiliated groups. But its influence may nonetheless determine the course of Turkey’s politics.

It has been revealed that the HDP’s decision not to field a candidate came just three days after head of the Republican People’s Party (CHP) Kemal Kilicdaroglu, Erdogan’s main rival, visited the party’s co-chairs. He told reporters that the solution to Turkey’s problems, “including the Kurdish problem” lies in parliament,” according to Turkish media.

Industry observers note that kilicdaroglu, who represents the six-party Nation Alliance opposition bloc, is the strongest contender to run against Erdogan in years. And while the HDP hasn’t yet announced whether it will put its weight behind him, analysts say it is the kingmaker in the elections.

Erdogan's 'polar opposite' wants to replace him as president of Turkey.

Recent findings suggest that “It was a carefully crafted political discourse,” Hisyar Ozsoy, deputy co-chair of the HDP and a member of parliament from the predominantly Kurdish province of Diyarbakir, told CNN. “We are not going to have our own candidate, and we will leave it to the international community to interpret it the way they wish.”.

Experts say the crackdown on the HDP is rooted in the threat it poses to Erdogan politically, as well as its position as one of the main parties representing Turkey’s Kurds, an ethnic minority from which a separatist militant movement has emerged.

The party and the Kurdish people have had a complicated relationship with Erdogan. The leader courted the Kurds in earlier years by granting them more rights and reversing restrictions on the use of their language. Relations with the HDP were also cordial once, as Erdogan worked with the party on a brief peace process with the PKK.

But ties between Erdogan and the HDP later turned sour, and the HDP fell under a sweeping crackdown aimed at the PKK and their affiliates.

Kurds are the biggest minority in Turkey, making up between 15% and 20% of the population, according to Minority Rights Group International.

It is unclear if the HDP will endorse Kilicdaroglu, but analysts say that the deliberate distance may be beneficial for the opposition candidate.

Sources indicate that the accusations against the HDP place it in a precarious position during the elections. It right now faces a case in Turkey’s Constitutional Court over suspected ties to the PKK, which is designated as a terrorist group by Turkey, the United States and the European Union. Knowing it may be banned at any moment, its candidates are running under the Green Left Party in parliament.

If the opposition is seen as allying with the HDP, Erdogan’s AK Party may use its influence in the media to discredit it as being pro-PKK, said Murat Somer, a political science professor at Koc University in Istanbul and author of Return to Point Zero, a book on the Turkish-Kurdish question in Turkey.

Sources indicate that the HDP’s threat to Erdogan’s hold on power became apparent after the June 2015 election, the first general election it participated in. It won 13% of the seats, denying the ruling AK Party its majority for the first time since 2002. Erdogan, however, called a snap election five months later, which led to a drop in the HDP’s support to 10.7%, as well as the restoration of the AK Party’s overall majority.

“They are a kingmaker in these elections because the HDP gets about half of the votes of the Kurdish population in Turkey,” mentioned Somer, adding that the other, more conservative Kurdish voters have traditionally voted for Erdogan’s AK Party. And last month, the Free Cause Party (HUDA-PAR), a tiny Kurdish-Islamist party announced support for Erdogan in the elections. The party has never won seats in parliament.

Erdogan's political fate may rest on his response to the earthquake.

The HDP knows that its position is key to the outcome of next month’s vote, but that it’s also in a delicate situation.

The Smart Ring Goes to Church

📅 20 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 7 min read (1352 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: WIRED

⏱️ ~7 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • Industry observers note that stressed?
  • The first generation of Christian smart rings is here, joining other religious wearables like iQibla’s dedicated Muslim smartwatches, rings, and Hajj bands alongside “kosher” smartwatch apps.
  • Everblessed’s $249 Elah Ring S1 went on sale in October and is shipping in the US.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Industry observers note that stressed? Heart rate elevated? If you’re wearing a smart ring from Oura, Ultrahuman, or Samsung, the spike could prompt app suggestions like breathing exercises, meditations, or a physical reset like a short walk. So far, so Silicon Valley. But now you can add reading the Bible to that list of self-soothing activities.

The first generation of Christian smart rings is here, joining other religious wearables like iQibla’s dedicated Muslim smartwatches, rings, and Hajj bands alongside “kosher” smartwatch apps. Two newly introduced devices in particular—Glorify’s Ring and Everblessed Technology’s Elah Ring—connect to hugely popular Christian prayer apps with tens of millions of consumers, and both claim to be the world’s first Christian smart ring.

Both are first, in their own ways. Everblessed’s $249 Elah Ring S1 went on sale in October and is shipping in the US. The $299 Glorify Ring introduced in July, with reservations open and shipping set for January 2027, but 77,000 units of an earlier beta iteration, the Amen Ring made by faith tech firm ConfideIn (which merged with Glorify this May), were given away last Christmas. Everblessed manages the Blessed app, and Glorify has an eponymous app.

Recent findings suggest that another substantial player in prayer apps is Hallow, aimed at Catholics, backed by Vice President JD Vance’s Narya venture capital firm and celebrity ambassadors, with 24 million installs to date. Hallow’s toe-dip into wearables was a 2024 smart rosary with NFC embedded in the crucifix, made with Italian brand Ghirelli; Everblessed tried an earbud, necklace, and bedside device before settling on the ring design.

Head-to-head on design, the Elah and Glorify rings are both made from titanium alloy, with a thorn-inspired twist for Glorify and a minimalist band featuring a cross for the Elah S1, which is also IP68 waterproof to 5 meters.

According to recent reports, for now, the Elah Ring is slightly techier: prayer reminders come via the cross, which glows via an LED, and “gentle” vibrations; these can pulse at certain times of day or be triggered by changes in heart rate and stress levels, picked up by a photoplethysmography (PPG) sensor. Glorify’s CEO Henry Costa tells WIRED these emotion-based reminders will land on the Glorify Ring in six months; for now, you can set the times of day you want prayer reminders, track heart rate, blood oxygen, stress, and sleep via the optical sensor.

One addition to the Glorify Ring that Costa indicates he personally uses “a lot” is recording prayers straight into the built-in mic. The ring has a light to signal when it's recording, and the app transcribes them. Everblessed CEO Ricky Xia says that, after consulting with pastors and users, the feeling was that voice notes on the ring were seen as “suspicious.” It’s available in-app, but most people don’t pray out loud, and too many features drain the battery life. (The Elah Ring runs for up to six days on one charge; Glorify for four to five days.).

Both companies see the smart ring nudges helping wearers prioritize meaningful quiet time, away from screens, while offering in-app Christian practices as an alternative to Eastern meditation. Glorify offers Bible study, courses, and meditations. Blessed has devotional “anchors,” Bible texts and audio, plus guided breathing. Xia claims he’s happy if the Elah vibrates and a user picks up a paper Bible rather than the Blessed app, while Costa says he’s “crying out to use my phone less.”.

Sources indicate that both Glorify (founded in 2020, now merged with ConfideIn and headquartered in the San Francisco Bay Area) and Blessed (founded in 2023 and based in San Jose) operate in more than 150 countries. Perhaps the biggest difference between the two rings is their relationship to AI.

It has been revealed that xia is all-in, describing the S1 as an “AI-native” product, with a pastor-complementing, not-replacing FaithMate chatbot in the Blessed app, customized based on preferences, congregation, and depth of learning. ChatGPT is like a “good coworker,” he says, while FaithMate is designed to be “your friend” and an agent that can also handle secular tasks.

Industry observers note that “A lot of our people not only ask questions about the Bible but also ask about themselves, their relationships with their wives, they’re being bullied at school," Xia says, stressing safeguards around data storage, encryption, and privacy. "Everyone is going to have some AI that they trust, and how they view that is built on their personal stuff, their private vulnerabilities.”.

Industry observers note that costa is more circumspect, treading carefully on the consumer-facing side and noting that the Pope has weighed in with a 6,000-word encyclical on AI. A launch interview with CBN News garnered negative comments: “AI is Antichrist Information,” for one.

“The stance I’ve always taken is that our daily devotional is hand-authored by a team of theologians,” Costa states. “It’s prayed over, and that is a stamp of approval.” He criticizes AI slop prayer apps as inauthentic. Still, he says the Glorify team has already tested “many forms” of AI personalization: “Any time, if we do use AI, it must be very clear to the user.”.

Smart ring owners were finding ways to add faith features to mainstream accessories before these rings came to fruition. For 20 years, timer and reminder apps have helped with prayer schedules, but recent examples are more creative. Heidi Campbell, professor of communication in religious studies at Texas A&M, refers to these DIY upgrades to the Oura ring and devices like the Muse headband as “spiritual mind-body hacking.”.

Oura owners on #christiantiktok chat about how they already use the ring’s stress and HR alerts as a prompt to pause and reflect, as per Elah.

Smart ring people flag changes in resting heart rate and sleep quality with scripture following their daily practice. “It’s really helpful for, like, what was inhibiting me from getting to a meditative or contemplative prayer state?” Campbell notes. “It takes some of the mystery out of prayer, I think, but that can also be positive. There is a way to do prayer well and not well.” Ring hackers can also dig into health stats during Lent, Ramadan, and Yom Kippur to analyze energy expenditure and how fasting periods affect their bodies.

AI-powered voice recordings and emerging attempts at emotion tracking are part of a fresh phase for smart rings, states Ekta Mittal, a senior analyst of connected devices at CCS Insight. These new “purpose-driven” features extend wearable tech into “new parts of consumers’ daily routines,” Mittal says. She suggests that while Glorify and Everblessed will add value for some, the rings are “not directly competing” with established smart ring giants like Oura, Ultrahuman, and Samsung.

It has been revealed that the pandemic sped up the digital transition of many places of worship when congregations could not meet up in person, encouraging experimentation with social media. So it’s early days for Silicon Valley’s impact on organized religion. Researchers at the University of Würzburg in Germany, led by Ilona Nord, are studying the theological implications of using tech, including smart rings, for spiritual practices, investigating which values are baked into secular devices and apps.

According to recent reports, campbell suggests many Christian groups haven’t stopped to consider the unintentional consequences of cultivating spirituality via personal tech. “All of these things are about individualizing the practice, which is good, but the challenges are for religions which are really focused on communal aspects,” she says. Not everyone has the money or connectivity to access these gadgets, but also, more existentially, “it puts spiritual development over communal development.”.

Xia points to the Blessed app’s communities, including its Healing Room broadcast feature, which lets pastors go live with sermons. It's not in the Elah app yet, but it's on the roadmap. Costa says communal practice is a core pillar, highlighting the “social layer” of public notes made on Christian texts in-app and an upcoming Glorify Ring feature which will allow a user to pair their device with a family member’s ring: “When your loved one is feeling down, you’ll get a buzz to check in with them.”.

iOS 27.3 Apple Intelligence, Siri AI usage limits: What to know

📅 20 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 7 min read (1308 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Mashable

⏱️ ~7 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • All good things must come to an end implement usage limits.
  • Just a few months after Apple finally launched the long-awaited Siri AI, its upgraded voice assistant powered by Apple Intelligence, the organization will now implement daily usage limits.
  • Sources indicate that what does this mean?
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

All good things must come to an end implement usage limits.

Just a few months after Apple finally launched the long-awaited Siri AI, its upgraded voice assistant powered by Apple Intelligence, the organization will now implement daily usage limits. These fresh restrictions will be implemented along with the launch of iOS 27.3.

Sources indicate that what does this mean? Basically, if a user hits those limits, they will need to upgrade their paid iCloud+ account or wait for the daily limits to reset. However, not every Siri AI request counts towards users' daily limits.

So, what counts towards your daily Siri AI limits? How much does it cost to upgrade? Lets break down everything you need to know about the fresh Siri AI usage limits.

According to Apple, "Siri AI and Apple Intelligence features are available for free for users with a supported device set to a supported language." However, "some features rely on powerful server models and have limits.".

Apple says the following features will have daily usage limits:.

Images: Intelligent Photo Editing Tools, which include Clean Up, Extend, and Spatial Reframing, as well as Image Playground.

Workflows and automation: AFM Cloud and AFM Cloud Pro models in Shortcuts.

Third-party apps that use Apple Foundation Models in Private Cloud Compute.

In a recent development, apple has not published exactly what the daily usage limits are for Apple Intelligence or Siri AI. The company's Support page simply describes it as a "generous daily usage limit.".

In a recent development, notably, each of those above categories has its own unique daily usage limits. These are not shared between those features, which means a user can hit the daily limit for one but not the others.

Daily usage limits are connected at the Apple account level and are implemented across all Apple devices, including iOS devices, Mac, and Apple TV.

According to recent reports, when a user reaches their daily limit, they will receive a prompt after making a request that counts towards those limits. Advanced requests are paused until the daily limit resets or the user upgrades to an iCloud+ proposal.

According to recent reports, "Daily Request Limit Reached," the prompt reads on iOS. "You can continue with basic requests.".

The prompt also includes a button to upgrade to an iCloud+ plan to increase those daily limits.

Industry observers note that as previously mentioned, Apple isn't sharing exactly what those Apple Intelligence and Siri AI limits are. However, they have shared just how many times those "generous" limits are increased when upgrading to an iCloud+ plan.

According to recent reports, here's an outline of what you get with each iCloud+ proposal: The best tech deal this week The Apple iPhone 18 Pro is free right now with T-Mobile Products available for purchase through affiliate links. If you buy something through links on our site, Mashable may earn an affiliate commission.

The Apple iPhone 18 Pro is free right now with T-Mobile.

200GB: $2.99 per month – Up to 2x daily usage limit.

2TB: $9.99 per month – Up to 5x daily usage limit.

6TB: $29.99 per month – Up to 10x daily usage limit.

12TB: $59.99 per month – Up to 20x daily usage limit.

The 50GB iCloud+ initiative, which Apple sells for $0.99 per month, does not include any increase in daily usage limits for Apple Intelligence and Siri AI.

Apple notes that all feature categories will have their daily limits reset at approximately midnight in the user's current time zone.

According to Apple, consumers who are travelling internationally will have their limits reset "around midnight in the central time zone of the country or region of your Apple Account." Users who share an iCloud+ plan with a Family Sharing group will see their limits reset at around midnight of the time zone of the iCloud+ plan purchaser. Users who aren't signed into their Apple Account will see their limits reset around 24 hours after they first used that feature category that day.

Unused limits from the previous day do not roll over.

Sources indicate that starting with iOS 27.3, Siri AI will also receive limits for certain "advanced" tasks. Apple indicates that basic tasks will continue to be unlimited and will work even when the daily usage limits for advanced tasks are reached.

You may be wondering what a "basic" task is and what is an "advanced" task, the latter of which will have daily usage limits.

Apple provided the following examples as a basic task, which owners will be able to utilize without limits:.

"Set a timer for three minutes.".

"Text Mark that Annika's party is at 123 Main Street.”.

As for advanced tasks, Apple provides these examples:.

"Text Mark the address for Annika's party, and tell him what time we need to leave from home to make it on time.".

"Add a summary of my San Francisco trip note to this email draft.".

Based on those examples, it appears advanced tasks involve multi-step requests that require server-side processing.

In a recent development, beyond Apple's official published examples, Apple leaker pdfu has uncovered Apple's more detailed instructions given to Siri AI telling the assistant how to decide if a user has reached their limits for advanced tasks. In an X post, the leaker explained Siri will take limits into account if a user request:.

uses information from one app, from what is on screen or from a message, in a different app, or needs a result from one step used in a different step or app (such as a looked-up fact typed into a field).

contains two or more separate asks in one sentence, even in the same app (extra details of one action, such as a cc or a time, are still one ask).

asks about or summarizes the content of a photo, a camera view or an attachment (editing, searching and albums are fine).

deletes, archives, junks, moves, marks or changes a set (all, every, these or a whole category) of the user’s emails, notes, reminders, messages, photos, files, contacts or events.

sets a device action or a notification to run on a time or trigger (not alarms, timers, reminders or calendar events), notifies someone when a person arrives or leaves, or builds or edits a Shortcut or automation.

is deep research or a multi-step task done on the user’s behalf.

asks you to compose or create newly introduced content (a story, poem, essay, strategy, recipe, image, or an email or message from a topic rather than wording the user gives), or to rewrite in a tone other than friendly, professional or concise.

A user asking a third-party AI assistant like ChatGPT for an advanced request is never limited, even if a user reaches their daily usage limit for the day.

According to pdfu, tasks like "proofreading, rewriting in a friendly, professional or concise tone, summaries as key points, a list or a table, typing or sending wording the user gives, a single direct operation in any app, even when Siri must look the target up first (the closest bakery, my cousin), 'this' or 'that' within its own app, running a Shortcut by name, a reminder for yourself by time or place, Find My, sharing your ETA or location, and all your home accessories (lights, doors, locks), alarms, timers or device settings" all fall under basic tasks.

In a recent development, so far, Apple hasn't released much more on these fresh daily usage limits for Apple Intelligence and Siri AI. Hopefully, before iOS 27.3 comes out, Apple provides users with more specific information regarding what does and doesn't count towards their daily usage limits.

Breaking: Dinosaurs may have been eating seaweed 100 million years ago

📅 15 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 6 min read (1203 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Sciencedaily

⏱️ ~6 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • Dinosaurs living along ancient coastlines may have enjoyed an unexpected addition to their diets: seaweed and other food from the ocean.
  • Today, powerful storms frequently deposit seaweed and other ocean material along shorelines, creating opportunities for animals that live on land to find additional food.
  • According to recent reports, A newly introduced study published in Frontiers in Ecology and Evolution suggests that this relationship between land and sea existed during the age of dinosaurs.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Dinosaurs living along ancient coastlines may have enjoyed an unexpected addition to their diets: seaweed and other food from the ocean. New research suggests that marine resources washed onto prehistoric beaches helped feed dinosaurs and their prey millions of years ago.

Today, powerful storms frequently deposit seaweed and other ocean material along shorelines, creating opportunities for animals that live on land to find additional food. Scientists call this process marine subsidization (MS). It is especially common in coastal environments and can become more important when food on land is limited, such as during droughts.

According to recent reports, A newly introduced study published in Frontiers in Ecology and Evolution suggests that this relationship between land and sea existed during the age of dinosaurs. By examining chemical signatures preserved in fossils, researchers found evidence that ocean resources contributed to prehistoric food chains.

Recent findings suggest that "We show that coastal terrestrial organisms in the greenhouse climates of the Cretaceous relied on marine resources to supplement their diets in a similar way that modern organisms do," said first author Dr. Clayton Forster, a geologist at the University of Arkansas. "We can identify that marine resources are passed along the food chain and incorporated in the minerals of bones and teeth of dinosaurs, crocodiles, turtles, and fish.".

Mysterious Chemical Clues in Dinosaur Teeth.

The discovery helps explain a longstanding mystery involving the chemical composition of dinosaur teeth.

According to recent reports, plants contain two forms of carbon known as isotopes: 'light' (C-12) and 'heavy' (C-13). Scientists can measure the relative amounts of these isotopes, expressed as δ13C, to identify a chemical fingerprint that passes from food into the animals that consume it.

As animals eat, this carbon signature becomes incorporated into their tooth enamel. The δ13C value in enamel is typically higher than that of the food consumed, with living animals generally showing an increase of between 11 and 13 parts per thousand.

Industry observers note that however, previous measurements of dinosaur teeth have consistently revealed unusually high values. These readings also exceed what scientists would expect from animals that ate only plants growing on land, which generally have lower δ13C values than most marine plants.

One possible explanation is that dinosaurs, or the animals they consumed, were obtaining some of their nutrients from the ocean.

"By determining the carbon isotope composition of dinosaur, fish, and crocodile tooth enamel, we can determine what their primary dietary source was and if they were different between regions," explained Forster.

Fossils Reveal a Prehistoric Ocean Food Source.

According to recent reports, to investigate, researchers examined fossils from (once) coastal locations bordering the Western Interior Seaway and the ancient coastline of the Gulf of Mexico. Around 100 million years ago, the Western Interior Seaway was an enormous inland sea that divided North America into two separate landmasses.

The team also analyzed fossils from locations farther inland, allowing them to compare animals that lived near the ocean with those that occupied landlocked environments.

The fossil deposits formed during two intervals of the Cretaceous Period: the early Albian (around 113-107 million years ago) and the early Cenomanian (approximately 100-96 million years ago).

Researchers used powdered fossil material to measure carbon isotope signatures from both periods. They also determined the latitudes where the animals had lived to investigate whether geography influenced the results.

A clear pattern emerged. Fossils from coastal environments consistently contained higher δ13C values than those from the inland formation. Remarkably, the coastal signatures remained similar across different locations, regardless of latitude or geological age.

These findings provide the first evidence of marine subsidization in prehistoric ecosystems, indicating that nutrients originating in the ocean were entering food chains on land millions of years ago.

Seaweed May Have Been on the Dinosaur Menu.

The researchers next considered what ocean food source could explain the widespread chemical signatures.

Recent findings suggest that "Coastal-dwelling organisms must have eaten some kind of organic matter from the ocean, or prey that had done so. This pattern is shared from fish to megaherbivores and indicates that the extra carbon source must have been low in the food-chain to affect both aquatic and terrestrial animals," Forster explained.

For the same chemical pattern to appear in such a wide variety of animals, the marine food source would likely have entered the food chain near its base. It also needed to be something that existed along coastlines but was absent farther inland, while remaining available for millions of years.

Seaweed emerged as the most likely explanation.

"Few organisms meet these criteria besides marine macroalgae or macrophytes - seaweeds," remarked Forster. "Given the almost ubiquitous behavior of large coastal herbivores today to supplement their diet with seaweeds, it's likely that most of the sampled herbivorous dinosaurs were no different.".

Modern plant-eating animals living near coastlines often consume seaweed to supplement their diets. The fossil evidence suggests that many herbivorous dinosaurs may have behaved similarly, with marine nutrients also passing to other animals through the food chain.

Not Every Dinosaur Had a Taste for the Sea.

Despite the widespread evidence of marine nutrients in coastal food webs, the researchers found that not every dinosaur took advantage of these resources.

One notable exception was Tenontosaurus tilletti, a large plant-eating dinosaur whose fossils have been discovered at numerous locations dating to the Cretaceous Period.

Its tooth enamel contained δ13C values comparable to those of modern animals that feed on plants growing on land. This suggests that Tenontosaurus tilletti did not rely on marine food sources, even though other dinosaurs apparently did.

According to recent reports, the difference also strengthens the researchers' interpretation of the fossil evidence. If geological processes occurring after death had altered the carbon signatures in dinosaur teeth, the same unusual values would be expected more broadly. Instead, the variation between species suggests that the elevated readings reflect genuine differences in diet.

An Ancient Connection Between Land and Ocean.

Although the findings provide strong evidence that marine resources supported the coastal ecosystems examined, important questions remain.

According to recent reports, the available fossils do not include specimens from polar or equatorial regions during the early Albian and early Cenomanian. As a result, scientists cannot yet determine how widespread this feeding behavior was across different latitudes.

Additional studies will also be needed to establish whether similar relationships existed during other geological periods, including the earlier Jurassic Period and the later early Cenozoic Era.

Beyond revealing a surprising possibility about what dinosaurs ate, the discovery highlights how closely life on land has been connected to the ocean throughout Earth's history.

"Our study emphasizes the connections between terrestrial and marine ecosystems," concluded Forster. "They are deeply intertwined and have been for hundreds of millions of years. It highlights the importance of environmental linkages across time and space and protecting them where they exist today.".

💡 Key Takeaways
  • Sources indicate that fresh manager, new formation, familiar defensive failings.
  • Yet for much of the second half, there had been reasons for Palace optimism.
  • Recent findings suggest that sometimes football is simply a bit daft, a series of events linked by very little discernible pattern – and that’s how it was before the break.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Sources indicate that fresh manager, new formation, familiar defensive failings. Twice Crystal Palace equalised. They seemed to have stabilised after half-time. But sometimes the rot is so deep-rooted that the new manager bounce manifests as nothing more than it not looking quite as shambolic as it did before. Thomas Frank started with a defeat that means Palace remain bottom of the table having lost five league games in a row.

Yet for much of the second half, there had been reasons for Palace optimism. They seemed to have settled better after a ludicrous first half in which neither side looked at all capable of defending. But a triple substitution by Frank Lampard with 20 minutes to go shifted the game back in Coventry’s favour. With five minutes remaining, a long throw arced into the box. Brandon Thomas-Asante headed it goalwards. Dean Henderson got in the way but the ball bounced off him, hit Dwight McNeil and ricocheted in. “We came through with spirit,” Lampard stated. “There was good play and a massive impact from the subs. It’s a good sign for the squad.”.

Recent findings suggest that sometimes football is simply a bit daft, a series of events linked by very little discernible pattern – and that’s how it was before the break. Perhaps that’s just what happens when two of the three teams with the lowest possession stats in the league meet up; they can’t both not have the ball and so at least one side ends up having to do something they’re not used to. The second half was rather less frenetic and rather more coherent, as Palace’s full-backs played more conservatively.

“There are more positives than negatives from the game,” remarked Frank. “Offensively we looked like a threat. The effort and mentality I was extremely happy with. Defensively we conceded the first goal in a situation we 100% should have defended better, then an individual mistake. We’ll keep working on it, keep reinforcing the message in terms of what we want to do.”.

In itself, playing without the ball is not a problem; absorbing pressure and striking on the break is a perfectly legitimate tactic and Lampard’s side have done it well at times this season. Palace are a slightly different case, given the obvious disconnect between their possession figure and Pierre Sage’s insistence he wanted to defend by holding the ball. That disparity, the sense that Palace’s players were unable to play as he wanted them to play, was probably the strongest argument in favour of cutting their losses promptly.

Frank abandoned the back three that had been the default not merely under Sage but also under Oliver Glasner, preferring a 4-3-2-1 with Anan Khalaili returning at right-back. It’s fair to say the Israel international is rather better going forward than at defending; playing at full-back rather than wing-back looked a real struggle for him – although he may feel there was mitigation in the way he was repeatedly left exposed. It took just five minutes for Coventry to open Palace up on that flank, three players converging on Yann Gboho as he backheeled a return pass to Jack Rudoni, who swept it across the box for Taiwo Awoniyi to stroke in.

• Coventry have won four of their last seven Premier League games (L3), with no side scoring more goals in the competition since the beginning of October (12, level with Bournemouth).

• Crystal Palace have conceded 27 goals in the Premier League this season; only in 1927-28 in the Third Division South have they conceded as many or more after 11 games in a league campaign (28).

• Only Brighton (6) have scored more goals from outside the box than Coventry City (4) in the Premier League this season, with 31% of the Sky Blues’ goals this term being scored from distance (4/13) – only Spurs (33% - 4/12) have a higher such share.

• In what was his 115th Premier League game as a manager, Frank Lampard (pictured) has been booked for the first time, while he also didn’t receive a single yellow card in any of his last 31 Premier League games as a player. Opta.

In a recent development, it soon became clear, though, that this was never a game of only one goal. It was startlingly, thrillingly, almost disconcertingly open, with chances at either end. Yéremy Pino levelled, thrashing in after Jørgen Strand Larsen had laid off Daichi Kamada’s overhit cross with an outstretched heel. Then Khalaili missed his tackle, allowing Rudoni to surge forward and square for Tatsuhiro Sakamoto who, from just outside the box, lashed the bouncing ball into the top corner. Palace’s second equaliser was the result of a complete defensive breakdown. Pino’s initial cross was blocked and when he dinked in a second attempt, the only player even close to marking Strand Larsen was his teammate Kamada.

Coventry’s threat had seemed diminished in the second half, partly as Palace looked less skittish and partly because Awoniyi aggravated an ankle injury and was unable to continue after the break. But those late substitutions gave them fresh impetus and, after a very silly first half, the game was won with a pretty silly goal.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Authorities have determined what led to Kimmarie Johnson’s death.

Recent findings suggest that two weeks after the actress, who appeared in Beverly Hills, 90210 and Dude, Where’s My Car?, died Nov. 3 following what her niece described as a “heart event,” her cause of death was determined to be cardiopulmonary arrest, according to a death certificate obtained by People, who listed her age as 59.

While a heart attack—medically referred to as myocardial infarction—is the result of a blocked artery, cardiopulmonary arrest—or cardiac arrest—is when the heart stops beating and is unable to effectively pump blood to the body, according to the Cleveland Clinic.

Johnson’s death certificate also listed an underlying cause as metastatic granulosa cell ovarian tumor with peritoneal carcinomatosis, meaning the rare type of ovarian cancer she had spread to her abdominal area, according to the Mayo Clinic.

After her death, Johnson’s niece Rhonda Scott reflected on the joy her aunt brought into the world.

It has been revealed that “She radiated a light so strong and bright,” Scott told People in an interview published Nov. 5. “People who came in contact with her felt nothing but positive energy. We will miss her tremendously and will continue to honor her life forever.”.

Johnson graduated from Wilkinsburg High School in Pittsburgh in 1985 before studying at California University in Pennsylvania. She won the title of Miss Pennsylvania USA in 1993 and was subsequently a finalist at the Miss USA pageant.

She later moved to New York City and then Los Angeles, where she pursued a career in modeling. While Johnson found small roles on the significant screen over the years, she launched her skincare brand SkinGlow by Kimmarie in 2011 and continued to model until her death.

She is survived by her son Cameron Nino, with whom she shared a special connection.

“My [son], u are bright, honest, kind, intelligent, funny and compassionate,” Johnson wrote on Facebook last November alongside a picture of her son for his 22nd birthday. “I’m glad that you enjoyed a good day.”.

💡 Key Takeaways
