📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Leeds dominate Chelsea for first Stamford Bridge win since 1999.

Chelsea manager Xabi Alonso is already in firefighting mode.

His team were booed by their own supporters at several points during a dominant 4-1 Leeds victory at Stamford Bridge, their first win there since 1999.

The first negative reaction came at half-time while the score was still 1-1. The ground then began to empty after the third and fourth Leeds goals, and the fans remaining voiced their dissent once more at the final whistle.

Although there were mitigating circumstances, including a potentially harsh penalty decision against them and the loss of midfielder Moises Caicedo to injury, joining a five-strong list of players on the treatment table, the defeat was thoroughly deserved.

It leaves Chelsea with three losses in their past four Premier League matches and they have slipped from fifth place to eighth, already 14 points behind league leaders Arsenal.

In October, Tottenham won at Stamford Bridge for only the second time in the Premier League era, while the 1-0 defeat at bottom club Sunderland before the international break was another alarm bell.

It is the first time in 67 years that Chelsea have lost at home to both Leeds and Spurs in the same season.

"We need to find solutions, for sure, because there will be setbacks during any game," Alonso noted after the match.

"To be able to go through that and to know that it's still so long to play, it's something mandatory in this competition and today I felt that probably we are in a fragile moment mentally.

"When we received a punch we didn't recover that strongly.".

Okafor double delivers rare win for Leeds at Chelsea.

'Officials can't use common sense' - was Rogers handball correct?

Indeed, even when Chelsea have been winning matches, they have often looked unconvincing.

Yet Blues supporters chanted their latest manager's name and seemed optimistic after the summer transfer business - despite a disappointing 10th-place finish last season.

Club record Â£117m signing Morgan Rogers was joined by the experienced trio of Emiliano Martinez, Danny Welbeck and Jordan Henderson.

It was the clinical finishing of Rogers, along with Cole Palmer and Joao Pedro earlier in the season, that masked the underlying fragility of Alonso's team.

Before this weekend, the Blues ranked 14th for expected goal difference and were joint 12th in Opta's expected points table.

After their latest setback, ex-England forward and BBC Match of the Day pundit Alan Shearer remarked: "Chelsea were all over the place. Once Moises Caicedo went off injured early on, there was no physicality and they looked weak.

Industry observers note that "They hardly created anything going forward and the back four didn't look comfortable. There was no desire, cohesion or fight from the home side, but we shouldn't take anything away from Leeds.

"Two weeks ago Chelsea were bullied by Sunderland centre-forward Brian Brobbey and they let Dominic Calvert-Lewin do the same today, which is alarming.

"It's fair to say Xabi Alonso's honeymoon period is over. He needs to tell his players this simply isn't good enough. They are miles off it and have to do better in every department.".

Xabi Alonso post-match interview - Chelsea v Leeds United.

Xabi Alonso was appointed Chelsea manager on a four-year deal in May.

In Alonso's defence, Chelsea had problems before his arrival.

They finished 10th last season, having been outrun in 37 of their 38 matches, and had three managers during a chaotic campaign.

Remarkably, Chelsea have seven more points from corresponding fixtures this season and last, but it mostly serves to show how low the bar was set.

Champions League qualification was again the club's pre-season target and Alonso's appointment was designed to bring stability and authority.

The former Real Madrid and Liverpool midfielder had an impressive playing career and earned much early admiration as a manager, guiding Bayer Leverkusen to a league and cup double in 2024.

However, the Spaniard, who was sacked by Real Madrid last season, has yet to establish any real consistency - beyond his defence leaking goals regularly.

Only Crystal Palace, Coventry City and Ipswich Town have conceded more goals than Chelsea this season.

Chelsea are also now averaging fewer than a goal per game since Joao Pedro suffered a thigh injury in training. Alongside Pedro and now Caicedo, Jorrel Hato, Maxence Lacroix, Reece James and Jamie Gittens are also injured.

It highlights how they have gained little benefit of having a season without European football.

Alonso is also beginning to face criticism from sections of the fanbase for both his team selections and substitutions.

Chief among the reasons is the constant chopping and changing of the starting XI, having now made 28 line-up changes (behind only Tottenham) while also switching between back-four and back-three systems.

In addition, Alonso is being criticised for his use of personnel, having deployed Pedro Neto as a striker on two occasions and, some would argue, not made enough use of exciting young winger Estevao.

Chelsea have shown 'no progression' under Alonso - Shearer.

Against Leeds he gave striker Emmanuel Emegha his first start alongside Estevao and, although the Dutch striker scored, the pair were the first players he substituted while Chelsea were chasing the game at 3-1 down.

Similarly, his late in-game interventions are under scrutiny, including the decision to bring on striker Welbeck only in the 90th minute of the defeat by Spurs.

He took until the 64th minute to make changes against Leeds when Chelsea were already 3-1 down. Only three clubs had made more substitutions in the last 15 minutes than Chelsea in the league this season.

Given Leeds' strengths, Chelsea should have been better prepared for what was coming. Before kick-off, Leeds had applied more high-intensity pressures in the opposition half than any other team in the Premier League.

It has been revealed that they had also generated the most expected goals from set-pieces and won the most duels. Leeds maintained those trends at Stamford Bridge against a Chelsea side often accused of being soft.

Chelsea have had problems in recent seasons, but this was still their worst home defeat since a 4-1 loss to Brentford in 2022.

Likewise, it is almost uncharted territory in Alonso's managerial career, having only previously lost at home by a three-goal margin once.

The stadium emptied and supporters again left early.

Players displayed negative body language and argued with one another both during the match and after the final whistle.

As a result, Alonso has gone from needing to fix defensive complications to dealing with problems that appear to be spreading throughout the squad.

#93574. MIT discovers that aging weakens the brain’s nighttime cleaning system

📅 18 Nov 2026 • ⏱️ 8m • 📚 Deep Dive (1673 w)

MIT discovers that aging weakens the brain’s nighttime cleaning system

📅 18 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 8 min read (1673 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Sciencedaily

⏱️ ~8 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • In a recent development, while we sleep, the brain carries out an essential maintenance process that helps wash away accumulated waste.
  • Sources indicate that researchers discovered that waves of cerebrospinal fluid (CSF), which help carry waste out of the brain, are significantly weaker in older adults.
  • According to recent reports, the findings raise important questions about whether weakened brain cleansing could contribute to Alzheimer's disease and other forms of dementia.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

In a recent development, while we sleep, the brain carries out an essential maintenance process that helps wash away accumulated waste. But latest research from MIT suggests that this natural cleaning system becomes less effective as we grow older, revealing another way aging can change the brain beyond simply disrupting sleep.

Sources indicate that researchers discovered that waves of cerebrospinal fluid (CSF), which help carry waste out of the brain, are significantly weaker in older adults. The decline appears to be connected to changes in the slow electrical waves that occur during deep sleep, as well as changes in how blood moves through the brain. Importantly, the reduced fluid movement cannot be explained simply by older people spending less time asleep.

According to recent reports, the findings raise important questions about whether weakened brain cleansing could contribute to Alzheimer's disease and other forms of dementia. The team now hopes to determine whether changes in these fluid waves could eventually help identify people at greater risk of cognitive decline.

According to recent reports, "We know that people age really differently. Some people age very successfully with great cognitive outcomes, and other people develop cognitive decline. If we can figure out who has great trajectories of aging and what are the factors that are associated with that, we might be able to use that to predict future outcomes," says Laura Lewis, the Athinoula A. Martinos Associate Professor of Electrical Engineering and Computer Science, a member of MIT's Institute for Medical Engineering and Science and the Research Laboratory of Electronics, and an associate member of the Picower Institute for Learning and Memory.

Lewis and her colleagues also want to investigate whether treatments or other interventions could strengthen this waste-clearing process in older adults.

In a recent development, the study was published in Nature Aging, with Lewis serving as senior author. Its lead authors are Sydney Bailes, a postdoctoral researcher in MIT's Laboratory for Information and Decision Systems, and Stephanie Williams, a former MIT visiting student who received her PhD from Boston University in 2026.

How Deep Sleep Helps the Brain Clear Waste.

Deep sleep does much more than leave us feeling refreshed. During its deepest stages, known as non-REM sleep, the brain produces powerful, slow electrical waves that support physical recovery, strengthen memories, and help regulate other essential functions.

In 2019, Lewis and her colleagues discovered that these slow brain waves also help generate rhythmic movements of cerebrospinal fluid. The fluid moves through spaces around the brain and plays an crucial role in carrying away waste products.

Sources indicate that that earlier discovery led to a newly introduced question. Because slow brain waves typically weaken with age, could the fluid movements responsible for clearing waste also become less effective?

Sources indicate that previous research had produced conflicting results. Some studies suggested that cerebrospinal fluid movement declined with age, while others reported increases. However, those investigations had not directly monitored the fluid during sleep, when the brain's natural cleaning activity is especially important.

It has been revealed that to investigate, the MIT team recruited two groups of volunteers. Younger participants were between 18 and 39 years old, while the older group ranged from 60 to 84.

Sources indicate that each volunteer completed a testing session lasting approximately two hours. The sessions began late at night, increasing the likelihood that participants would become sleepy during the measurements.

The researchers combined several techniques to observe what was happening inside the brain. Functional magnetic resonance imaging, or fMRI, allowed them to track changes in cerebral blood flow. A specialized MRI method developed by Lewis measured cerebrospinal fluid movement, while electroencephalography, or EEG, recorded the brain's electrical activity.

Many participants fell asleep inside the scanner, providing an opportunity to compare their brain activity and fluid movements during wakefulness and sleep.

According to recent reports, the results revealed a striking age difference. As younger adults entered non-REM sleep, their slow brain waves grew stronger and were accompanied by larger waves of cerebrospinal fluid. In older adults, however, the average fluid waves were substantially smaller.

The findings showed that aging was associated with a weakening of the fluid movements that normally accompany deep sleep.

Why the Aging Brain's Cleaning Waves Weaken.

Sources indicate that the researchers next investigated what might be causing this decline. In a separate set of experiments conducted while participants were fully awake, they examined how the brain's blood vessels responded to different demands.

One possible explanation involved neurovascular coupling, the process that connects brain activity with blood flow.

Industry observers note that when a particular region of the brain becomes more active, its cells require additional oxygen and nutrients. Nearby blood vessels normally widen to deliver more blood, ensuring that the active cells receive the resources they need.

To measure this response, the researchers demonstrated volunteers a flickering checkerboard pattern while monitoring blood flow with fMRI. The rapidly changing visual pattern stimulates activity in regions involved in processing vision, which should trigger an increase in local blood supply.

Sources indicate that in many older participants, the brain's electrical activity increased as expected, but the corresponding rise in blood flow was much smaller. This suggested that aging had weakened the ability of blood vessels to respond to the brain's changing oxygen requirements.

The team then performed a second experiment to examine the brain's broader vascular responsiveness.

Participants were instructed to hold their breath while researchers monitored changes in cerebral blood flow. Holding one's breath causes carbon dioxide to accumulate in the bloodstream, which normally prompts blood vessels in the brain to widen and increase blood flow.

Once again, the older group revealed a weaker response. On average, their cerebral blood flow increased less than it did in younger volunteers.

Together, these experiments indicated that changes in the brain's vascular system could help explain why its waste-clearing fluid waves diminish with age.

Using a statistical model, the scientists found that weakened neurovascular coupling and reduced blood flow responses accounted for much of the decline in cerebrospinal fluid movement. However, the two mechanisms did not explain the entire difference, suggesting that additional biological changes associated with aging are also involved.

"Aging is so complex, and so many different things change, that it's really hard to disentangle the individual factors," Bailes states. "We try to account for some of the mechanisms, but there definitely are a lot of other factors related to vascular health and lifestyle. If you were able to measure all of them, you might be able to break it apart into different explanations for why an individual's CSF flow might be more or less impaired.".

Could Weaker Brain Cleansing Increase Dementia Risk?

The discovery may have important implications for understanding neurological diseases associated with aging.

Earlier studies have linked disrupted sleep to a greater risk of Alzheimer's disease and other forms of dementia. Because cerebrospinal fluid helps remove waste from the brain, researchers are particularly interested in whether age-related changes in its movement might contribute to neurodegeneration.

None of the volunteers in the MIT study had been diagnosed with a neurodegenerative disorder. However, brain scans revealed that some older participants indicated signs of gray matter atrophy, meaning a loss of brain tissue in regions containing large numbers of nerve cells.

Those changes were associated with greater reductions in cerebrospinal fluid movement.

Recent findings suggest that the relationship does not establish that weakened fluid flow causes brain tissue loss or dementia. Nevertheless, it provides a reason to investigate whether these changes might serve as early warning signs of neurological decline.

The researchers hope to follow some of the participants over time to determine whether reduced cerebrospinal fluid movement is associated with a greater likelihood of developing a neurodegenerative condition.

Can the Brain's Nighttime Cleaning System Be Restored?

Beyond understanding why brain cleansing declines, the MIT team is exploring whether it might be possible to improve the process.

One promising possibility involves sound stimulation during sleep.

Recent findings suggest that in a separate recent study, Lewis' laboratory found that brief bursts of "pink noise" could increase cerebrospinal fluid movement in younger adults. Pink noise is a type of sound that contains a broad range of frequencies, with greater emphasis on lower frequencies than white noise.

Although the approach has shown potential in younger people, researchers have not yet tested whether it can produce similar effects in older adults.

Another intriguing finding could provide clues about how to preserve the brain's natural cleaning abilities.

Sources indicate that while older participants generally had weaker cerebrospinal fluid waves than younger adults, the decline was not universal. Some older volunteers retained fluid movements that were comparable to those measured in healthy younger people.

This raises the possibility that certain biological or lifestyle factors may help protect the brain's waste-removal system against aging.

"It's really intriguing that for some of these older adults, their CSF fell right in the range of the healthy young adults," Lewis indicates. "We are really interested in what's different in those people and how that might be related to future health outcomes.".

Understanding why some older brains maintain these youthful fluid movements could ultimately help researchers identify ways to support healthier brain aging and investigate whether preserving the brain's nighttime cleaning system can reduce the risk of cognitive decline.

The research received funding from the National Institutes of Health, the Simons Collaboration on Plasticity in the Aging Brain, a McKnight Scholar Award, a Pew Biomedical Scholar Award, an MIT EECS Transformative Research Award, the Picower Institute Neurological Disorder Discovery Research Fund, a Sloan Fellowship, and the Department of Defense National Defense Science and Engineering Graduate Fellowship Program.

Breaking: Borussia Dortmund bows to fan pressure and end Rheinmetall deal

⏱️ ~4 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • Two years of fan pressure and criticism has forced Borussia Dortmund to drop a sponsorship deal with Germany's largest arms manufacturer, Rheinmetall.
  • The Bundesliga club will not renew its deal with Rheinmetall beyond its expiry in June 2027, at the end of this season.
  • "It reduces our financial room for manoeuvre.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Two years of fan pressure and criticism has forced Borussia Dortmund to drop a sponsorship deal with Germany's largest arms manufacturer, Rheinmetall.

The Bundesliga club will not renew its deal with Rheinmetall beyond its expiry in June 2027, at the end of this season. Dortmund chairman Carsten Cramer confirmed the news on the club's website ahead of its AGM on Sunday, which may have proved a potential flashpoint. He acknowledged that "our partnership has been controversial from the outset" but lamented the loss of income.

"It reduces our financial room for manoeuvre. We will have to reprioritize planned investments and carefully examine how we can find viable solutions.".

Though he welcomed the news, one of the leaders of the fan revolt against the partnership, Michael Schulze von Glaser, warned this is likely not the end of the road.

To view this video please enable JavaScript, and consider upgrading to a web browser that supports HTML5 video.

"I think in the end it was a victory for the fans. But I'm also a bit skeptical about  what the future will bring us," the Dortmund fan and former head of the German Peace Society told DW. "Football fans in Germany always must be skeptical and always must watch what the club is doing.”.

Recent findings suggest that many Dortmund fans have opposed the deal — which has seen Rheinmetall's logo on advertising boards and other surfaces at locations such as Dortmund's 83,000-capacity Westfalenstadion — from its beginnings in 2024. It was estimated to be worth between €7 ($7.68 million) and €9 million per year.

At the club's AGM that year, 556 of 855 members present voted against the deal in a non-binding vote. There were 247 votes in favour, with 52 abstentions. This, said Cramer, informed the eventual outcome.

Industry observers note that rheinmetall sells arms mostly to Germany, Ukraine and NATO but fans and critics feel that platforming any arms manufacturer goes against the club's statement of its core values. In that, Dortmund states its desire for "a club and a society that operate free of racism, anti-Semitism, LGBTQIA+ hostility, sexism, violence and discrimination.".

To play this audio please enable JavaScript, and consider upgrading to a web browser that supports HTML5 audio.

It has always been clear, said Schulze von Glaser, that this deal did not chime with that.

Sources indicate that "In the end, they kill people. They are for war," he mentioned of Rheinmetall. "The slogan of Borussia Dortmund is true love (Echte Liebe). But for me and many others, our love ends there…. I know some fans who have put fan merchandise in the trash because they were so shocked.”.

According to recent reports, in the Q and A on the club's website, Cramer said he was still a "personal advocate" of the deal but that Dortmund's commitment to the 50+1 model, which means German clubs are majority controlled by the members, meant they had to listen to fan voices. But he also warned that Rheinmetall must be an "absolute exception and an isolated case.".

That set off some alarm bells for Schulze von Glaser.

"It's a bit concerning that there are constantly these attacks on professional football — a upcoming sponsorship, investment deals," he remarked.

Industry observers note that indeed, Dortmund's climbdown is not the first of its kind in Germany's top flight. Last year, after fan and media pressure, Bayern Munich ended its commercial deal with the tourism arm of the Rwandan government before its conclusion.

Fans had objected to the promotion of Rwanda, which many felt sought to divert attention from its poor human rights record and actions in the war with DR Congo, through sporting partnerships. Two years earlier, Bayern withdrew from a similarly controversial deal with Qatar Airways.

Elsewhere in the league, Werder Bremen fans objected to their long time shirt sponsor, Wiesenhof. Many supporters took issue with the factory farming practices  of Germany's largest poultry producer. Though it was not given as a direct reason for the end of a shirt sponsorship deal in 2023, it likely played a part.

In a recent development, union Berlin fans have also made their voices heard. When the club signed a upcoming shirt-sponsorship deal with Luxembourg real estate tech giant, Aroundtown, upon promotion to the top flight in 2019, many fans were frustrated at the tie up in a city where rent prices were skyrocketing.

"It's a problem for a lot of people," fan Sven Dobberstein told DW at the time.

"We have to try to find a way between commercialization and what we have at the moment. It isn't easy.".

Striking that balance can often be a source of tension for Bundesliga clubs. 50+1 ensures fans have a voice, preventing rich owners, or nation states, from taking control as they do in England's lucrative Premier League or in France or Spain. Indeed fan protests have also stopped the league signing a €1billion private equity partner and seen Monday night matches scrapped. For Schulze von Glaser, this needs to be protected.

"In Germany, the fan culture has an impact," he said.

”If there is something bad or terrible happening in your club and in the Bundesliga, there are the organized fans and they can have an impact if they want, if they stand together and, yes, they can stop the Rheinmetall deal.".

Additional reporting by: Emmie Eernisse.

Beauty for $1 billion, she had the perfect response for internet trolls claiming she used a word that doesn’t exist.

In a screenshot shared to her Instagram Stories Nov. 20, Bieber shared the dictionary definition of “optimistical,” which is described as “a version of optimistic.”.

Clapping back at those who gave her some flak for using the word, the 29-year-old wrote over the image, “anyways….”.

Bieber made the remark during her appearance at the Newly introduced York Times’ DealBook Summit in New York City Nov. 18, where she shared further insight into the May 2025 sale of her beauty company.

Sources indicate that “A billion dollars was the number that I mentioned I would not sell it for less than that,” she said. “That felt crazy, that’s like shooting for the stars, stars, stars, stars, stars.”.

As for what made the goal possible, the beauty mogul credited “delusion.”.

She added, “You have to have a certain sense of optimistical delusion I think.”.

Soon after her remarks, internet users took to social media to criticize Bieber over her word choice.

"'Optimistical' my eye is twitching," one user wrote on X, while another added, "Why does she think 'optimistical' is a word.".

“I think there’s a resilience that you build,” she explained at the summit, “with so much time of enduring and going through such intense scrutiny and being so perceived all the time.”.

“I’m just someone who pays attention,” she continued. “I’m not that girl that can be like, ‘Yeah, I’m just gonna ignore it.’ I don’t work that way. I’m too sensitive and I care too much to try to be that person that it doesn’t bother me.”.

But pouring herself into her work makes dealing with criticism a bit easier.

“I’m an entrepreneur at the end of the day,” she told TIME in an interview published April 30. “I want to expand in business, and I want to be able to do more things—but I’m definitely not in a rush.”.

💡 Key Takeaways

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Teenager Williams-Barnett shines as Spurs beat Ipswich.

Luca Williams-Barnett's performance in his first Premier League start was that good it had two of his Tottenham team-mates labelling him "incredible".

The 18-year-old winger delivered the opener with his first senior goal and then played a pivotal role in Dominic Solanke's second as Spurs comfortably beat Ipswich 2-0 at home.

As full debuts go, it does not get much better than that.

Yet what might be a sign of the excitement about his potential was manager Roberto de Zerbi calmly explaining that "his talent is bigger than this performance".

The Tottenham boss obviously believes this is just the beginning for the talented teenager.

Williams-Barnett became the youngest Spurs player to score in the Premier League since Gareth Bale against Fulham in September 2007.

They would be pretty impressive footsteps to follow in if he was to get close to the player Bale once was for the north London club.

But for the slightest of touches on his fizzed ball across the area from Ipswich goalkeeper Christian Walton before Solanke turned home, Williams-Barnett would have become the second-youngest player ever to both score and assist in a Premier League game, aged just 18 years and 51 days old.

Only Michael Owen, who did it at 17 years and 364 days for Liverpool in 1997, would have done it at a younger age.

"He's incredible, honestly," Solanke told Final Score. "We get to see him every day in training so we know what a player he is - the confidence he has, the ability he has.

In a recent development, "The world got to see it today, which is great for him. His confidence and ability is amazing. He'll help us a lot.".

'Unbelievable' - How Spurs youngster Williams-Barnett impressed on first start.

Williams-Barnett was born in Luton and played for his hometown club before moving to Spurs at the age of 10.

The teenager has been generating excitement with his performances for the club's underage teams for some time.

Back in the 2023-24 season, he played for Tottenham's Under-18s aged just 15 and in the following campaign he scored the Under-18 Premier League goal of the season against Leicester having become renowned for fine long-range strikes.

Williams-Barnett has been around Tottenham's first-team since the 2024-25 campaign as he was on the bench for three Europa League games and a Premier League match but his debut came last season as a substitute in a Carabao Cup game against Doncaster Rovers under previous boss Thomas Frank.

Last December, he scored five goals in a Under-19 UEFA Youth League game against Slavia Prague.

But this season looks to be his real breakthrough.

Williams-Barnett featured in the EFL Cup as a substitute in a 5-1 victory over Charlton in August before coming off the bench against Crystal Palace and Leeds in the Premier League.

Yet it was still a bold choice from De Zerbi to make Williams-Barnett the club's sixth youngest starter in Premier League history given Spurs were coming into this game on the back of a defeat by Leeds United which checked a recent upturn in form.

However, the Spurs boss was rewarded with a man-of-the-match worthy display.

His goal was one of endeavour as he brushed in front of Ipswich defender Abdoul Ouattara to reach Pedro Porro's cross and become the club's youngest scorer on their Premier League full debut.

Throughout the game, he was looking for the ball constantly and not afraid to run with it and try to make things happen.

"Obviously I am so happy for him, every day in the training session he demonstrates his quality," Tottenham defender Destiny Udogie told BBC Match of the Day.

Recent findings suggest that "Honestly he's just an incredible football player. I hope he keeps doing what he's doing.".

The winger was unfortunate not to get the assist but the goal does not happen without his powerful cross.

The England youth international was not afraid to take on a shot and his four attempts were all on target while he had a passing accuracy of 77.4% among his 44 touches.

Only Solanke took on more shots in the game with four of his five on target.

"To see him come in and do that on his first Premier League start is crazy," added Solanke.

"He's a great person and is obviously still young, you know what young boys are like.

"But he's very dedicated and so brave on the ball which is great, in his position I think you need that.".

Roberto De Zerbi post-match interview - Tottenham Hotspur v Ipswich Town.

Williams-Barnett was replaced by Savio in the 64th minute which brought a standing ovation from the crowd but, with the Brazilian then being forced off later on with an injury, there may be more opportunities in the coming weeks.

Obviously there will be more excitement about the talented teenager now which De Zerbi will have to manage and he has picked midfielder James Maddison as a good mentor for the attacker.

"He's played very well, but his talent is bigger than this performance," the Spurs boss told BBC Match of the Day.

"It was the first game and I am very happy, I am very delighted for his performance, but he is a big, big, big talent.

In a recent development, "The management of the younger talented players is different because you can't take risks to lose their enthusiasm and their positive mentality. But I think Tottenham's dressing room now is a good environment for him.

"I put [James] Maddison to play very close to him to speak the same language but also to help him and put him in the best conditions to play. To play with freedom, to play with his qualities because his qualities are very massive.

"He has to work hard but also he has to keep the passion to keep the love of football.".

'He's incredible' - Solanke praises Spurs teenager Williams-Barnett.

Teenager Williams-Barnett inspires Spurs to win over Ipswich.

Industry News: Uranus and Neptune’s bizarre magnetic fields may finally be explained

📅 15 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 6 min read (1121 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Sciencedaily

⏱️ ~6 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • When NASA's Voyager 2 spacecraft visited Uranus and Neptune in the 1980s, it discovered something extraordinary.
  • In a recent development, now, researchers believe they may have found an answer hidden deep inside these enormous worlds.
  • The research, published in Communications Physics, was led by scientists at The University of Texas at Austin in collaboration with researchers from the University of California, Los Angeles, Imperial College London, and Northumbria University.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

When NASA's Voyager 2 spacecraft visited Uranus and Neptune in the 1980s, it discovered something extraordinary. Unlike Earth, which has a relatively orderly magnetic field with clearly defined north and south poles, both distant planets possess strangely distorted and dramatically tilted magnetic fields. For decades, scientists have struggled to explain why.

In a recent development, now, researchers believe they may have found an answer hidden deep inside these enormous worlds. A newly introduced study suggests that changes in how well materials conduct electricity under extreme conditions could explain the planets' unusual magnetism. The findings also raise an intriguing possibility: the magnetic fields of Uranus and Neptune may change dramatically over just a few decades.

The research, published in Communications Physics, was led by scientists at The University of Texas at Austin in collaboration with researchers from the University of California, Los Angeles, Imperial College London, and Northumbria University.

Why Uranus and Neptune Have Such Strange Magnetic Fields.

It has been revealed that planetary magnetic fields originate deep beneath the surface, where moving fluids capable of conducting electricity generate magnetic forces. Scientists call this process a dynamo.

Recent findings suggest that on Earth, the dynamo operates within the outer core, a layer of molten metal surrounded by mostly solid rock. As liquid iron circulates and the planet rotates, it generates a magnetic field resembling that of a giant bar magnet. This produces the familiar north and south magnetic poles that allow compasses to point in a consistent direction.

Earth's magnetic field is also closely aligned with its rotation axis. Its main magnetic axis, known as a dipole, is tilted by only 11 degrees. Uranus and Neptune are strikingly different. Uranus has a magnetic dipole tilted by 59 degrees, while Neptune's is tilted by 47 degrees.

Explaining these extreme tilts requires a better understanding of what lies inside the two planets.

According to recent reports, uranus and Neptune are classified as ice giants, a name that reflects their presumed composition rather than suggesting they are simply frozen worlds. Each is approximately four times wider than Earth, and scientists believe their interiors contain substantial amounts of hydrogen, helium, water, ammonia, methane, and rocky material. However, their precise internal compositions remain uncertain.

Extreme Conditions Deep Inside the Ice Giants.

Chi Yan, the study's lead author and a research associate at the UT Jackson School of Geosciences, believes the combination of the planets' enormous size and unusual chemical makeup may help explain their distorted magnetic fields.

"Deep inside Uranus and Neptune, pressures and temperatures become extremely high," remarked Yan. "Under these conditions, which can cause water molecules to break apart into ions, the material may become increasingly electrically conductive with depth.".

Sources indicate that ions are electrically charged particles that can carry electric current. If the materials inside Uranus and Neptune become more conductive at greater depths, that could significantly influence how their magnetic fields are generated.

To investigate this possibility, the researchers developed computer simulations designed to reproduce the strange magnetic fields recorded by Voyager 2.

Their models assumed that electrical conductivity increases deeper inside the planets. The researchers also tested a variety of possible internal structures, examining how circulating fluids, temperature changes, and magnetic forces interact over time.

The results suggest that these changing electrical properties could play a crucial role in producing the unusual magnetic fields observed around both ice giants.

Magnetic Poles Could Shift Dramatically Within Decades.

Perhaps the most surprising finding is that the magnetic fields of Uranus and Neptune may be far less stable than Earth's.

According to the simulations, their magnetic axes could undergo substantial changes in relatively short periods. In some scenarios, the magnetic tilt shifted by tens of degrees within only a few decades.

That raises the possibility that the magnetic fields surrounding Uranus and Neptune today are significantly different from those measured when Voyager 2 flew past them in the 1980s.

Recent findings suggest that "Earth's magnetic tilt drifts by only a degree or so over 50 years," noted Yan. "Our models show the ice giants can behave very differently. In some stretches the tilt swings by tens of degrees within decades. In others it shifts only slightly over the same span.".

These dramatic changes remain predictions from computer models rather than confirmed observations. However, scientists may already have a way to look for evidence of them.

James Webb Telescope Could Reveal Magnetic Changes.

Researchers are now examining detailed infrared images of Uranus and Neptune captured by the James Webb Space Telescope (JWST). They are particularly interested in the planets' auroras, which form when charged particles from the Sun interact with gases in their atmospheres.

According to recent reports, auroras are closely connected to planetary magnetic fields, making them valuable clues to what is happening far above the planets' hidden interiors. Changes in the appearance and arrangement of these glowing atmospheric features could help researchers determine whether the magnetic poles have shifted since Voyager 2's encounters.

"We are busy working on what's contained within these observations, but the shape and structure of the aurora, as well as other weird patterns in the ionosphere, promises to provide us with a way of understanding how the magnetic fields have changed, an important stepping stone," said Tom Stallard, a professor at Northumbria University who led the JWST observation campaign and reviewed the paper for the journal.

The ionosphere is a region of the upper atmosphere containing electrically charged particles. Its behavior is influenced by magnetic activity, offering another potential source of information about the planets' changing magnetic environments.

It has been revealed that the research team hopes to combine Webb's auroral observations with Voyager 2's original magnetic field measurements and the upcoming dynamo simulations. Together, these sources of evidence could provide the clearest picture yet of how the magnetic fields of Uranus and Neptune are arranged today.

Even so, scientists emphasize that fully understanding the planets' deep interiors will require fresh spacecraft missions to these distant worlds. Until then, improved simulations and powerful telescopes may help unravel one of the solar system's most unusual magnetic mysteries.

The research was funded by The University of Texas Institute for Geophysics (UTIG) in the Jackson School of Geosciences, the National Aeronautics and Space Administration (NASA), and the Science and Technology Facilities Council.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Research funding opportunities across Europe are receiving record numbers of applications.Credit: Ulrich Baumgarten via Getty.

According to recent reports, swastik Chowbey, an astrophysicist at the University of Milan in Italy, spent three and a half months preparing his application for the prestigious Humboldt Research Fellowship. On 14 November, he stayed up through the night completing the form and coordinating with referees across different time zones.

Recent findings suggest that after sending his application to his prospective academic host in Germany for final checks, Chowbey took a break to go hiking. When he returned to submit it at around 8.50 p.m., applications had closed. The fellowship had reached its limit of 800 applications within 21 hours of opening.

Chowbey is not alone. Many researchers around the world found themselves unable to submit applications last Sunday and took to social media to vent their annoyance.

“It is incredibly frustrating to invest so much time and effort into developing a strong scientific project, only to discover that the timing of the application process may put some researchers at a disadvantage — especially when you open the system on Sunday and close it the same day,” wrote Ida Skubis, an AI researcher at Silesian University of Technology in Gliwice, Poland, on the social-media platform LinkedIn.

The Humboldt Research Fellowships support researchers from abroad to conduct research in Germany, providing €3,000 (US$3,300) a month for postdoctoral researchers and €3,600 a month for experienced researchers. Fellowships can last for 6–24 months for postdocs and 6–18 months for experienced researchers.

The fellowships and awards are recognized internationally, which is why they are so competitive, says Marcela Hernández, an environmental microbiologist at the University of Birmingham, UK, and a former fellow. “Being a Humboldtian is a mark of academic distinction. It has an exceptional international network.”.

Industry observers note that A spokesperson for the Alexander von Humboldt Foundation in Bonn, Germany, noted in a statement to Nature that it had not anticipated that the application cap would be reached within 24 hours of opening. The foundation introduced the cap this year because it has seen a large increase in applications since 2024. It holds application rounds in March, July and November.

According to recent reports, the spokesperson noted that as more researchers have used AI to help prepare their applications more swiftly, the volume of applications has increased. Humboldt does not prohibit the use of generative AI in applications, nor are applicants required to declare AI use.

Simon Hammann, a chemist at the University of Hohenheim in Stuttgart, Germany, supported a research proposal as a prospectiveacademic host for someone who was able to submit their application successfully. He notes that opening the call on a Sunday disadvantaged researchers with family and caring responsibilities. “That should definitely be changed.”.

The Humboldt spokesperson mentioned that the foundation advertises the date when applications will open, but that unfortunately the date fell on a Sunday this time.

“We recognize the impact this had on those who were unable to apply, particularly given the challenges of coordinating availability over a weekend. We sincerely apologize for the disappointment and frustration this has caused,” the spokesperson said.

They added: “We will take this as an opportunity to continue reflecting on and improving our processes” to “find a transparent and fair solution”.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

It has been revealed that BLYTHEWOOD, S.C. — Electric vehicle startup Scout Motors has notched roughly 212,000 reservations for its upcoming EVs as the manufacturer nears completion of its latest $2 billion plant here, CEO Scott Keogh told CNBC.

The reservations are for the Volkswagen-backed firm's Terra pickup truck and Traveler SUV, which are expected to start full production next year before deliveries begin to customers in 2028.

In a recent development, reservations do not necessarily translate to sales, as the U.S. automotive industry has learned during the past decade, especially with highly anticipated all-electric trucks such as the Ford F-150 Lightning, Tesla Cybertruck and others that garnered strong interest that didn't lead to meaningful numbers of purchases.

Keogh stated he expects Scout could roughly double those reservations by the time customer production begins, but he said the more notable thing is to convert early interest into actual sales as production nears.

Industry observers note that "It's been a consistent drumbeat," Keogh said during an interview at Scout's plant site outside Columbia. "I think we could easily be up over 400,000 with reservations without doing too much effort. The massive thing for us is how much of the initial production can we 100% presell.".

Industry observers note that keogh stated achieving an order book of 12 to 18 months "would be great" and is something he thinks the organization can do before production. Scout on Thursday said plant construction is "in its final phase.".

Scout's vehicles will be offered as all-electric versions as well as electric hybrid variants, known as extended-range electric vehicles, or EREVs, that include an internal combustion engine as a backup generator for the electric motors and batteries.

Scout, a former American vehicle brand from 1961 to 1980, was expected to exclusively offer EVs in a bid for the German automaker to expand its presence in the U.S. However, slower-than-expected adoption of EVs and higher costs led the firm to decide to offer EREVs as well.

Keogh said extended-range and SUV models are dominating reservations thus far, with roughly 87% choosing EREV models and 75% being SUVs.

Recent findings suggest that the CEO also stated the tech giant is drawing interest from its target markets, which include owners of off-road vehicles such as the Ford Bronco and Jeep Wrangler as well as full-size pickup trucks and U.S. EV leader Tesla.

It has been revealed that given the interest signaled by reservations, Keogh said the tech giant is expected to launch with the EREVs first, followed by the EVs. He also said the company plans to launch with mid-level models first, a deviation from many companies that begin with their highest-priced models.

Recent findings suggest that both the Traveler and Terra are expected to start at under $60,000. The EREV models are expected to feature more than 500 miles of range, according to the tech giant, compared with 300 miles of range for the all-electric models.

In a recent development, "The No.1 thing for me is I want to go get the best volume as soon as possible," Keogh said. "In my mind, it's how quick can you get to 100,000 units? It's at 100,000 units where you can start to punch through.".

His comments come months after Rivian Automotive received criticism online for launching its R2 SUV with its highest-priced models first, despite that being a common practice across the automotive industry.

Keogh said Scout's South Carolina plant is about 85% complete, but supporting infrastructure and a $300 million supplier park continue to be installed.

Reservations for Scout's vehicles initially opened in October 2024, when it revealed the Traveler and Terra, which feature sleek, yet rugged, exteriors that pay some homage to the brand's historic models.

💡 Key Takeaways
  • SpaceX's 35th Dragon cargo mission has come home to Earth.
  • In a recent development, the robotic Dragon capsule undocked from the International Space Station (ISS) on Friday (Nov.
  • The freighter made its way Earthward over the next 29 hours, ultimately splashing down in the Pacific Ocean off the coast of California on Saturday (Nov.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

SpaceX's 35th Dragon cargo mission has come home to Earth.

In a recent development, the robotic Dragon capsule undocked from the International Space Station (ISS) on Friday (Nov. 20) at 12:05 p.m. EST (1705 GMT), while the duo were flying 260 miles (418 kilometers) above western China.

The freighter made its way Earthward over the next 29 hours, ultimately splashing down in the Pacific Ocean off the coast of California on Saturday (Nov. 21) at 5:03 p.m. EST (2155 GMT).

In a recent development, the Dragon launched Oct. 13, on a mission called CRS-35 because it was the 35th that SpaceX has flown for NASA's Commercial Resupply Services program.

The capsule arrived at the ISS on Oct. 15, delivering more than 6,300 pounds (2,860 kilograms) of food, scientific gear and other supplies to the astronauts aboard the orbiting lab. It brought a lot of stuff down to Earth, too.

Industry observers note that "Thousands of pounds of cargo are returning from the space station, including research samples that could advance future space exploration and improve life on Earth," NASA officials wrote in an revision on Tuesday (Nov. 17).

"The returning research includes a 3D-bioprinted blood vessel construct scientists used to study vascular aging and cardiovascular disease in space and on Earth," they added.

Dragon is the only cargo craft flying today that's capable of making such downward deliveries. The others — Northrop Grumman's Cygnus, Russia's Progress vehicle and Japan's HTV-X — are all expendable and burn up in Earth's atmosphere to wrap up their first and only spaceflight.

Editor's note: This story was updated at 12:20 p.m. ET on Nov. 20 with news of successful undocking, then again at 8:55 p.m. ET on Nov. 21 with news of splashdown.

📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • In a recent development, A virus that infected chimpanzees millions of years ago has left behind a genetic legacy that may help explain an notable difference between human and chimpanzee brain development.
  • In a recent development, the findings, published in Science Advances, reveal how infections from the distant past can leave lasting changes in the genetic makeup of an entire population.
  • Sources indicate that although pandemics are often considered a modern threat, infectious diseases have been spreading through large animal and human populations for millions of years.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

In a recent development, A virus that infected chimpanzees millions of years ago has left behind a genetic legacy that may help explain an notable difference between human and chimpanzee brain development. Researchers at Lund University have discovered that ancient viral DNA embedded in the chimpanzee genome switches off a gene that remains active in humans and appears to play an important role in the developing brain.

In a recent development, the findings, published in Science Advances, reveal how infections from the distant past can leave lasting changes in the genetic makeup of an entire population. They also offer newly introduced clues about how the brains of humans and our closest evolutionary relatives may have developed differently.

Sources indicate that although pandemics are often considered a modern threat, infectious diseases have been spreading through large animal and human populations for millions of years. Some of these ancient infections left traces of viral DNA that continue to influence how genes function today.

Johan Jakobsson, Professor of Molecular Neurogenetics at Lund University, says the discovery demonstrates how a virus can introduce genetic changes that eventually become widespread throughout a population.

It has been revealed that "The virus we investigated specifically affected chimpanzees. Yet humans and chimpanzees have largely the same genetic makeup. That is why it is important to understand the differences in how genes are regulated. Our findings suggest that one gene, LINC00662, plays a significant role in early human brain development," indicates Johan Jakobsson.

How an Ancient Virus Silenced a Brain Development Gene.

It has been revealed that at the center of the discovery is a gene called LINC00662. Researchers found that it is active during early human brain development but completely switched off in comparable chimpanzee brain models.

The difference appears to be caused by a genetic remnant of PTERV1, an ancient virus that infected chimpanzees millions of years ago. PTERV1 belongs to a group known as endogenous retroviruses, which are viruses whose genetic material became incorporated into the DNA of their hosts. Once embedded in the genome, these viral sequences can be inherited by future generations.

It has been revealed that over time, PTERV1 produced numerous copies of its genetic material that became scattered across different parts of the chimpanzee genome. Researchers found that these viral sequences are systematically silenced through a process called methylation.

Methylation involves chemical modifications to DNA that help regulate gene activity. It is one of the ways cells control which genetic instructions are used and which remain inactive. In this case, the ancient viral insertion appears to have caused a neighboring gene involved in brain development to be switched off.

Jakobsson says understanding these differences in gene regulation could also provide important insights into how genetic activity protects the brain or contributes to damage and disease.

Miniature Brains Reveal a Striking Genetic Difference.

It has been revealed that to investigate the virus's effects, researchers grew miniature brain models called organoids using stem cells from humans and chimpanzees. These three-dimensional structures reproduce certain features of developing brain tissue, allowing scientists to study aspects of early brain development under controlled laboratory conditions.

When the team compared the two types of organoids, the difference was striking. LINC00662 demonstrated strong activity in the human brain models but was completely inactive in those derived from chimpanzee cells.

"The gene was strongly expressed in the human organoids, but not at all in the chimpanzee organoids," indicates Patricia Gerdes, postdoc in molecular neurogenetics at Lund University.

The researchers then set out to determine whether the ancient viral DNA was directly responsible for this difference.

Using CRISPR-Cas9, a powerful gene editing technology that allows scientists to make targeted changes to DNA, they removed the viral sequence from chimpanzee cells.

The result provided compelling evidence. Once the viral DNA was removed, the previously inactive LINC00662 gene switched back on.

"This shows that it is in fact the viral insertion that is responsible for the gene being switched off in chimpanzees," says Patricia Gerdes.

New Clues to Human Brain Evolution.

The team also wanted to understand what LINC00662 actually does in the human brain. To investigate, they used CRISPR to switch off the gene in human brain organoids and examined how other genes responded.

In a recent development, disabling LINC00662 reduced the activity of genes associated with nerve cell development and the formation of connections between neurons. These processes are essential for establishing the networks that allow the brain to communicate and function.

The results suggest that LINC00662 contributes to key stages of early human brain development, while the ancient viral insertion prevents the gene from functioning in chimpanzees.

In a recent development, more broadly, the discovery highlights an key principle of evolution. Although humans and chimpanzees share much of their genetic material, differences in how genes are switched on and off can influence how their bodies and brains develop.

The findings suggest that ancient viral infections may have contributed to these differences by altering gene regulation long after the original infections disappeared.

Recent findings suggest that researchers now strategy to investigate whether other remnants of ancient viruses have similarly influenced brain evolution. They also hope to determine whether these inherited viral sequences may play a role in neurological diseases.

Together, the discoveries raise an intriguing possibility that some of the differences between human and chimpanzee brains may trace back, at least in part, to viruses that infected our evolutionary relatives millions of years ago.

David Raya has made 163 appearances since joining Arsenal in 2023.

Injuries are never good news, but Arsenal's latest one to first-choice goalkeeper David Raya has come in the worst possible position.

The 31-year-old was forced to leave the pitch 70 minutes into Saturday's 2-2 draw with Newcastle, appearing to hurt his shoulder in an innocuous challenge with Magpies forward William Osula.

The Gunners arguably have the best depth in the league with at least two quality options in all outfield positions after a period of squad strengthening.

In goal, however, cover appears much thinner.

Raya was a key component in Arsenal's Premier League title-winning campaign last season, was named in the Fifpro Men's World 11 and was unlucky to not win the Yashin Trophy, awarded to the world's best goalkeeper, which went to Spain team-mate Unai Simon.

Behind him, Kepa Arrizabalaga still holds the record as the most expensive goalkeeper in football history following his Â£72m move from Athletic Bilbao to Chelsea in August 2018, but is far behind Raya in terms of quality.

Raya's passing range and ability on the ball are key to how Arsenal build their attacks, and his presence is a massive reason why they have the best defence in the league.

They have conceded just seven Premier League goals this season, with only Brighton able to match that tally - having played a game fewer.

Arsenal also brought in former Leeds goalkeeper Illan Meslier on a free transfer in the summer but his only appearance this season came in the embarrassing Carabao Cup defeat by League Two Fleetwood.

When asked about Raya's injury, Arteta remarked he did not know how severe the glitch is.

"Well, unfortunately, he had to come off, which is never good news," remarked Arsenal manager Mikel Arteta.

"He will get assessed now, and probably he will have an MRI [scan] tomorrow to see what it is exactly he has done.

"I don't know how it happened, and what the injury is at the moment, so we'll have to wait and see tomorrow.".

In a recent development, who was 'a consistent threat'? Newcastle v Arsenal player ratings.

Arsenal go six clear after lively draw at Newcastle.

Arsenal are about to enter a gruelling period of games - with or without Raya.

In the next four weeks, they face Borussia Dortmund, Manchester City, Brentford, Tottenham Hotspur and Real Madrid.

"The one player that Arsenal cannot afford to lose is David Raya," mentioned former England forward Alan Shearer, who is a pundit on Saturday's BBC Match of the Day. "He has made such a difference since joining from Brentford in 2023.

Recent findings suggest that "They have top-class cover in just about every other position but he is the one individual that Mikel Arteta will be thinking 'we don't want to play without him for an extended period'. They could, of course go into the transfer market if they need to in January, but Arteta will be desperately hoping Raya is not out for long.".

Raya is reportedly close to agreeing a fresh deal at the club, which shows his importance to the Gunners with two years remaining on his contract.

Ex-England midfielder Jamie Redknapp said on Sky Sports that Raya is "irreplaceable".

In a recent development, "Kepa is not up to the level of him - I actually think he struggles in the Premier League," added Redknapp. "Obviously we've seen in the Carabao Cup last year in the final.

"He is now going to have to play some games and that's going to be difficult for him.

"It will change everything for Arsenal for a while so that's a massive blow depending on how long David Raya is out because he is irreplaceable - probably the best goalkeeper in the Premier League, if not one of the best in the world.".

No one feels the electric touch of Taylor Swift and Karlie Kloss’ reunion quite like Jennifer Lawrence.

Industry observers note that after the Grammy winner and supermodel came together to cheer on Swift’s husband Travis Kelce as his Kansas City Chiefs took on the New York Jets at Arrowhead Stadium on Nov. 8, the Hunger Games alum shared her theory as to why the pair finally reached a state of grace after years of feud rumors.

Sources indicate that “That’s what happens when you get old,” Lawrence quipped to Andy Cohen during her Nov. 19 appearance on Watch What Happens Live. “The things that you fought about, like it just seem silly.”.

As she put it, “It just seems like elder abuse to me.”.

Though Swift, 36, and Kloss, 34, proved there’s no bad blood while cheering on the “Opalite” hitmaker’s guy on the Chiefs earlier this month, that wasn’t always the case.

In fact, speculation surrounding their friendship began after the former Victoria’s Secret Angel’s name was noticeably left off a T-shirt that Swift wore in her 2017 music video for “Look What You Made Me Do”, which featured a list of her girl squad.

And though Kloss attempted to calm down the speculation by sharing a photo with Swift backstage at the Reputation tour in 2018, the “I Knew It, I Knew You” singer did not attend Kloss’ wedding to Kushner—with whom she shares kids Levi, 5, Elijah, 3, and Rae, 13 months—a few months later.

At the time, no one was more concerned with the big reputation of their friendship than Lawrence.

"I'd like to know what's going on with Karlie Kloss and Taylor Swift, that's the honest to God truth,” the Silver Linings Playbook actress said in a 2018 interview with The Newly introduced York Times. "Is nobody else curious? It's keeping me up at night. What happened?”.

In a recent development, but it seems their friendship is safe and sound these days. After all, Kloss was even in attendance for the latest chapter in Swift and Kelce’s love story as they tied the knot at Madison Square Garden July 3.

And while Kloss was hush-hush about the ins and outs of the ceremony, she made it all too clear that she and Swift’s friendship has seen daylight once again.

Recent findings suggest that “Listen, I try to protect the privacy of my friends’ personal lives,” Kloss noted on Today July 28. “But what I will say is that they’re an amazing couple and I’m so happy for them.”.

May the odds be ever in your favor as you keep reading for more of Lawrence’s best quotes….

When she was nominated for her first Best Actress Oscar at 20, for the 2010 indie drama Winter's Bone, Jennifer Lawrence made quite the impression right out of the gate, setting the tone for endless interviews to come.

"I just ate a Philly cheese steak and I was kinda worried about it," the star, clad in her instant-classic red Calvin Klein dress, shared with Entertainment Tonight on her first Oscars red carpet when told she looked incredible.

It has been revealed that "You know, I think that people are built the way that they're built," she continued. "You know, there's that quote, the Kate Moss quote, that's like 'Nothing tastes as good as skinny feels'? "And I'm like, I can name a lot of things that taste better than skinny feels: potatoes, bread...a Philly cheese steak and fries!".

This is not the outfit Lawrence was wearing when, in her words, she stalked John Stamos at a party.

"He was at a party, and I turned into a perverted guy," she remarked on Conan in 2013. "I was like following him into rooms and staring at his ass.".

Lawrence explained, "I lost my mind. And I got so upset—I didn't want to meet him because when I meet people it's never good, and I was avoiding him. But then my friends brought him over because my friends are jerks, and I started really freaking out. And he asked me if I was on mushrooms and I said, 'No. I'm dead sober. This is just me...'.

"I just kept smiling and being like, 'Dude... Uncle Jesse.'".

Nick Jonas alerted Stamos to the interview by tweeting at him, "I envy you," to which Stamos replied, "I envy myself!" The Full House star added, "For the first time, I was totally oblivious.".

"You guys are just standing up because you feel bad that I fell—and that's really embarrassing, but thank you," the Silver Linings Playbook star said upon finally reaching the stage to accept her Oscar for Best Performance by an Actress in a Leading Role in 2013, making the 22-year-old the second-youngest best actress winner ever.

Though the incident did indeed establish her reputation as a stumbler, the standing ovation was for a role well played.

And maybe a little bit because she fell.

"Was that on purpose? Absolutely," Lawrence joked backstage, Oscar in hand. "What do you mean, 'what happened?' Look at my dress," she added, pointing to the massive skirt of her Dior ballgown. "I tried to walk upstairs in this dress. That's what happened...Yeah, I think I just stepped on the fabric, and they wax the stairs.".

Asked what went through her mind in that moment, she replied, "A bad word that I can't say, that starts with 'F.'".

Recalling the moment a year later to W, Lawrence explained, "I was at the Oscars, waiting to hear if my name was called, and I kept thinking, Cakewalk, cakewalk, cakewalk. I thought, Why is 'cakewalk' stuck in my head? And then, as I started to walk up the stairs and the fabric from my dress tucked under my feet, I realized my stylist had told me, 'Kick, walk, kick, walk.' You are supposed to kick the dress out while you walk, and I totally forgot because I was thinking about cake! And that's why I fell.'".

Lawrence later wondered if the fall was the beginning of a descent.

She already felt that her perch at the top of the Hollywood food chain was "precarious," noting on the Newly introduced York Times' The Interview podcast in 2025, "That’s just the nature of things.".

According to recent reports, "And then I fell getting my Oscar," she continued, "and the next year I was waving to fans and I tripped on a cone and I remember being like: “[Expletive], that’s it. Nobody’s gonna believe that I fell two years in a row.”.

So, when she was accused of staging a fall, "Everybody thought that meant everything that I did was fake and it was all a shtick. This is how it felt to me. That I got found out as this fraud.".

Whether she knew she was in the frame or not, the Hunger Games star zeroed in on Taylor Swift at the 2014 Golden Globes with a flourish.

"I was going to come in and push you down the stairs," Lawrence quipped when she crashed Swift's interview with E!'s Ryan Seacrest. "I was like, 'She'll crack up. She would really love that.'".

We haven't stopped thinking about Lawrence calling the crease that naturally forms under one's arm her "armpit vagina" at the 2014 SAG Awards.

Lawrence had a raging crush on Larry David, but you could almost hear the "...eh" coming from the Seinfeld and Curb Your Enthusiasm creator.

"I'm in love with him, and I have been for a very long time," she told Vanity Fair in 2014. "I worship Woody Allen, but I don't feel it below the belt the way I do for Larry David.".

In a recent development, when those quotes were read back to him during a Fresh Yorker Festival Q&A, David, who's 43 years her senior, replied, "I don't think I could do it. On one hand, it's very flattering and on another hand, it's kind of a shame—in terms of timing. I'd have fun watching the reality show of it, though.".

Her love for the Real Housewives franchise is real, so of course she and her pals made a sojourn to the since-shuttered Pump in West Hollywood, part of Lisa Vanderpump's restaurant empire, where they created their own intro for spin-off Vanderpump Rules.

Someone was excited to see the iconic funnyman making his Comic-Con debut in 2015.

According to recent reports, "I've been a major fan of Bill Murray for a really long time," Lawrence told reporters at a press conference following the cast's Mockingjay Part 2 panel in Hall H. "I sent emails to Woody, mostly when I was drunk, about things I always wanted to say to Bill Murray. So, he received them. The fact that Bill Murray knows that I exist was part one, part two was, he wanted to speak to me.".

Lawrence made no secret of her obsession with the reigning first family of reality TV, even revealing that she watched endless repeats of Keeping Up With the Kardashians while shooting mother! so she could decompress from the intense role.

It has been revealed that she told Vogue in 2017, "It got to a point in the movie where it got so dark I was like ya know what? I need the Kardashians.".

Cue Lawrence FaceTiming into KUWTK in 2019.

Rules of the sky be damned, Lawrence commandeered the mic to lead her fellow airplane passengers in a cheer for the Philadelphia Eagles ahead of Super Bowl LII—which they won.

How She Really Felt About Her Wedding Day.

"I'm so happy I didn't freak out and cancel the wedding and run away and go, 'I'll never be taken down!'" Lawrence cracked to the New York Times in 2021.

But, in all honesty, "It's so stressful," she told E!'s Keltie Knight at the 2024 Golden Globes about the day she wed gallerist Cooke Maroney in 2019. "You're not having fun. You're just like, 'Is that person having fun?'".

Asked what she'd been up to during her acting hiatus, the visibly pregnant Lawrence told Stephen Colbert in December 2021, "I just had a ton of sex.".

Why She Took a Break From Hollywood.

Sources indicate that “I was not pumping out the quality that I should have,” Lawrence, who put acting on the back burner in 2018 after several of her films in a row were met with underwhelming responses, told Vanity Fair in 2021. “I just think everybody had gotten sick of me. I’d gotten sick of me. It had just gotten to a point where I couldn’t do anything right. If I walked a red carpet, it was, ‘Why didn’t she run?’".

Why She Identifies as a "Stay-at-Home Mom".

Industry observers note that “I identify as a stay-at-home mom," Lawrence, who shares two young sons with husband Cooke Maroney, remarked on a January 2026 episode of SmartLess. "But I am obviously working.".

Industry observers note that she explained, “I’m not used to being busy like this. I normally have a busy three months while I’m filming, but even in that sense, it’s calm because there is nothing else to do. I just go to work, come home, sleep, and then I do it again. And then, for two weeks, you promote. It is hectic.”.

In a recent development, "There’s no squeezing [in work] when you have a baby," Lawrence told fellow mom Cameron Diaz in a chat for Interview in 2024. "There’s just home, and it’s the best. It definitely helps weed out projects: 'Yes. No. Yes. No. Yes. No. Is this worth being away from my child for half the day?'".

"Fortunately," she added, "my husband is the greatest father in the entire world, so when I’m working, I don’t have any more guilt than the usual every day, all-day parent guilt.".

It has been revealed that "I'm giving it a shot," Lawrence remarked in a Sept. 10, 2026, video announcing her presence on Instagram as @jlaw after avoiding social media forever. "And if anyone claims anything negative, I will quit. Immediately. No questions asked.".

In a recent development, she further warned, "If anyone thinks something mean, I'll know. I'll know, and I'll quit.".

Cosmetic Procedures & Plastic Surgery.

Lawrence is intrigued by various procedures, but for now she needs to makes sure she can look up (and down, to the side, etc.).

"I need to have movement in my face—I get baby Botox, but I can't do a lot," she told Vogue in an interview published Sept. 3, 2026. "If my skin is going to be a little saggier than I would like, at least it looks dewy and pretty.".

And she's admittedly curious but "really nervous about these fat transfers" that she sees other people doing, explaining, "I support other people doing them because I want to continue to watch and see what happens, but I don't know about that. I mean, I would love to have a buccal fat removal. I can't because everybody would know, but just know that I want that.".

“The moment something was fussy, it was like ‘no,’” Lawrence explained to The Cut in an October 2026 interview about the vibe behind her new hair care brand Mes (pronounced mess). “Avoiding pretentious words and pretentious font is significant. Our girl is not that. But she appreciates beauty.".

According to recent reports, and, Lawrence admitted, "I want to be a sexy mom. At drop-off, I want to look like a woman that has her s--t together even when I’ve just woken up and don’t have my s--t together.”.

#93558. Latest Update: Physicists defy expectations by controlling the magnetic heart of a single atom

Latest Update: Physicists defy expectations by controlling the magnetic heart of a single atom

📅 16 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 5 min read (965 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Sciencedaily

⏱️ ~5 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • Sources indicate that researchers at Delft University of Technology (The Netherlands) have accomplished something that physicists previously thought should not be possible.
  • The findings, published in Nature Communications, also present scientists with a upcoming puzzle.
  • Industry observers note that atoms in magnetic metals such as iron and nickel behave like tiny magnets.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Sources indicate that researchers at Delft University of Technology (The Netherlands) have accomplished something that physicists previously thought should not be possible. Using radio waves, they managed to directly control the magnetic spin of the nucleus inside a single atom. The unexpected result challenges existing assumptions about how atomic magnetism behaves and could eventually lead to new ways of storing and retrieving quantum information.

The findings, published in Nature Communications, also present scientists with a upcoming puzzle. Although the experiment demonstrated that this remarkable level of control is possible, researchers do not yet fully understand the mechanism that makes it work.

The Hidden Magnetism Inside Every Atom.

Industry observers note that atoms in magnetic metals such as iron and nickel behave like tiny magnets. However, the magnetism within an atom comes from different sources. Both electrons and, in some cases, the atomic nucleus possess a quantum property called spin, which can be thought of as a miniature magnetic compass needle.

Sources indicate that "By far the strongest magnetism comes from the electrons," claims lead researcher Sander Otte. "But in some atoms, the nucleus also carries a spin. That spin is much weaker, but it is also much better shielded from the outside world.".

Recent findings suggest that that protection makes nuclear spin especially interesting to quantum researchers. Because it is less exposed to disturbances from its surroundings, it could offer a promising way to preserve delicate quantum information.

To investigate these tiny magnetic properties, Otte's team uses a specially modified scanning tunneling microscope. This powerful instrument allows the researchers to deliver electrical signals to individual atoms with extraordinary precision.

According to recent reports, until recently, their experiments concentrated primarily on electron spin because it is easier to detect and measure. The nucleus's magnetic spin could only be observed indirectly through a phenomenon known as the hyperfine interaction, which creates a subtle quantum connection between the spins of the electron and nucleus. This connection can cause the two spins to become slightly entangled, meaning their quantum states are linked.

An Atomic Experiment Produces an Unexpected Result.

Sources indicate that in the latest study, lead author Hester Vennema and her colleagues took a different approach. They simultaneously applied two separate signals to a single atom, with one directed at the electron and the other at the nucleus.

Sources indicate that by using these signals together, the researchers could investigate their effects independently. What happened next caught them by surprise.

According to recent reports, even when the electron and nuclear spins were largely disentangled, the team was still able to flip the orientation of the nucleus's magnetic spin. Based on their previous understanding, the nucleus should not have responded in this way.

In a recent development, "According to our simple understanding, this should not really happen," states Otte. "The nuclear spin should not be sensitive at all to the electrical signals from a scanning tunneling microscope.".

The result suggests that the interaction between electrical signals and nuclear spin involves a mechanism that scientists have yet to fully explain.

Controlling Quantum Spins Like Guitar Strings.

In a recent development, achieving this level of precision required the researchers to adapt a technique called double magnetic resonance so it could operate on a single atom. The method allowed them to manipulate the magnetic behavior of the atomic nucleus separately from that of an electron.

It has been revealed that magnetic resonance works by applying a wave signal at a carefully selected frequency to change the orientation of a magnetic spin. However, quantum mechanics restricts these changes to specific allowed transitions, meaning the frequency must be precisely matched to the spin being targeted.

Vennema compares the process to playing a musical instrument.

Industry observers note that "You can compare it to the strings of a guitar," Vennema explains. "Each possible spin rotation is like a string with its own note. You have to play precisely the right note to make a particular string vibrate. The "notes" of a nuclear spin are a hundred to a thousand times lower than those of an electron spin.".

In other words, electrons and atomic nuclei respond to very different frequencies, much as different guitar strings produce different musical notes. By tuning their signals to the appropriate frequencies, the scientists could address the two types of spin separately.

A Quantum Breakthrough With a Mystery Still to Solve.

The discovery could have notable implications for the future of quantum information technology. Unlike conventional computers, which store information as bits representing either 0 or 1, quantum systems can use quantum states to encode information in more complex ways.

One major challenge is keeping those states stable long enough for information to be stored and retrieved reliably. Nuclear spins are attractive candidates for quantum memory because they are relatively well isolated from environmental interference.

In a recent development, the ability to control these spins directly could therefore open new possibilities for writing, storing, and reading quantum information. However, the findings represent an early experimental advance rather than a ready-to-use quantum memory technology.

For now, one of the most important outcomes is the new scientific mystery the experiment has revealed. The researchers have demonstrated an unexpected way to manipulate nuclear spin, but the physical mechanism responsible remains unclear.

"Back to the drawing board, then," says Otte. "That is really how science works. There is always something new left to figure out.".

Is the AI bubble bursting just as Anthropic goes public?
